units.zh: 顧和，字君孝，侍中衆之族子也。
units.en: Gu He, whose courtesy name was Junxiao, belonged to a cadet line of Gu Zhong, the former Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Gu He, courtesy name Junxiao, was a collateral descendant of Gu Zhong, who had served as Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 曾祖容，吳荊州刺史。
units.en: His great-grandfather Rong had served Wu as regional inspector of Jing Province.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Rong had been Inspector of Jing Province under Wu.

units.zh: 祖相，臨海太守。
units.en: His grandfather Xiang had been governor of Linhai commandery.
units.literal: His grandfather Xiang had been Administrator of Linhai.

units.zh: 和二歲喪父，總角便有清操，族叔榮雅重之，曰：「此吾家麒麟，興吾宗者，必此子也。」
units.en: Orphaned at two, he showed moral clarity while still a child. His uncle Rong thought the world of him and declared, “Here is our clan’s qilin—this boy will restore our house.”
units.literal: He lost his father at age two; even as a boy wearing his hair in tufts he showed pure conduct. His clansman uncle Rong held him in high esteem and said, “This is our family’s qilin; the one who will raise up our lineage must be this boy.”

units.zh: 時宗人球亦有令聞，為州別駕，榮謂之曰：「卿速步，君孝超卿矣！」
units.en: Another kinsman named Qiu was already known as capable and held the post of provincial aide. Rong told him bluntly, “You may be quick on your feet, but Junxiao will leave you behind.”
units.literal: At that time another clansman, Qiu, also had a fine reputation and served as Provincial Aide. Rong said to him, “You move fast, but Junxiao will outpace you!”

units.zh: 王導為揚州，辟從事。
units.en: Wang Dao, while heading Yang Province, recruited Gu He onto his staff.
units.literal: When Wang Dao governed Yang Province, he summoned Gu He as an aide.

units.zh: 月旦當朝，未入，停車門外。
units.en: On the day of the first court session of the month, before going in, he drew up his carriage outside the gate.
units.literal: On the monthly dawn audience he had not yet entered; he stopped his carriage outside the gate.

units.zh: 周顗遇之，和方擇虱，夷然不動。
units.en: Zhou Yi came upon him as he sat picking lice from his robe, perfectly composed.
units.literal: Zhou Yi encountered him; Gu He was picking lice from his clothing and remained utterly unmoved.

units.zh: 顗既過，顧指和心曰：「此中何所有？」
units.en: When Zhou Yi walked past, he turned back, tapped Gu He’s breast, and asked, “What have you got in there?”
units.literal: After Yi had passed, he turned and pointed at Gu He’s chest, saying, “What is inside here?”

units.zh: 和徐應曰：「此中最是難測地。」
units.en: Gu He replied calmly, “This is the spot no one can easily read.”
units.literal: Gu He answered slowly, “This is exactly the place that is hardest to fathom.”

units.zh: 顗入，謂導曰：「卿州吏中有一令僕才。」
units.en: Zhou Yi went in and told Wang Dao, “One of your provincial aides has the makings of a chief minister.”
units.literal: Yi entered and said to Dao, “Among your provincial clerks there is one with the talent of a chief minister.”

units.zh: 導亦以為然。
units.en: Wang Dao agreed.
units.literal: Dao likewise thought so.

units.zh: 和嘗詣導，導小極，對之疲睡。
units.en: On one visit to Wang Dao, the minister was mildly indisposed and dozed off in Gu He’s presence.
units.literal: Gu He once visited Dao; Dao was slightly unwell and fell asleep facing him.

units.zh: 和欲叩會之，因謂同坐曰：「昔每聞族叔元公道葉贊中宗，保全江表。
units.en: Gu He considered rousing him and remarked to the others, “We always heard my uncle Yuanda praise Emperor Zhongzong’s cooperation with him and how together they kept the south secure.
units.literal: Gu He wished to wake him and therefore said to those seated with him, “I have often heard how my clansman Uncle Yuanda assisted Emperor Zhongzong with his virtue and preserved the lands south of the Yangzi.

units.zh: 體小不安，令人喘息。」
units.en: Even a slight indisposition in such a man was enough to take one’s breath away.”
units.literal: When his body was slightly unwell, it made one catch one’s breath.”

units.zh: 導覺之，謂和曰：「卿珪璋特達，機警有鋒，不徒東南之美，實為海內之俊。」
units.en: Wang Dao woke, overheard him, and said, “You are cut from exceptional stuff—sharp and perceptive. You are not only the best the southeast has to offer; you rank among the finest in the empire.”
units.literal: Dao woke, heard him, and said to Gu He, “You stand apart like fine ritual jade—you are alert and incisive; you are not merely the finest of the southeast but truly eminent within the realm.”

units.zh: 由是遂知名。
units.en: From that moment his name was made.
units.literal: Thereupon he became known.

units.zh: 既而導遣八部從事之部，和為下傳還，同時俱見，諸從事各言二千石官長得失，和獨無言。
units.en: Soon Wang Dao dispatched eight department aides on inspection tours; Gu He came back from the outer circuits with their reports and was admitted with the rest. Every aide aired complaints about the commandery governors—only Gu He stayed silent.
units.literal: Presently Dao sent out eight department aides on inspection tours; Gu He returned as courier from the lower districts and was received together with them. Each aide spoke of the merits and faults of the two-thousand-shi officials; Gu He alone said nothing.

units.zh: 導問和：「卿何所聞？」
units.en: Wang Dao pressed him: “What did you hear?”
units.literal: Dao asked Gu He, “What have you heard?”

units.zh: 答曰：「明公作輔，寧使網漏吞舟，何緣采聽風聞，以察察為政。」
units.en: Gu He replied, “You govern as chief minister—surely the net may let the great fish slip rather than you chase gossip and rule by nit-picking.”
units.literal: He answered, “You, sir, assist the throne—better that the net let great fish escape than that you heed rumor and govern by picky scrutiny.”

units.zh: 導咨嗟稱善。
units.en: Wang Dao sighed his approval.
units.literal: Dao sighed with admiration and praised him.

units.zh: 累遷司徒左曹掾。
units.en: He advanced step by step to secretary in the Minister of Education’s left section.
units.literal: He rose through successive appointments to aide in the Left Bureau of the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 時東海王沖為長水校尉，妙選僚屬，以沛國劉耽為司馬，和為主簿。
units.en: While the Prince of Donghai, Chong, held the colonelcy of the Changshui encampment, he handpicked his staff, naming Liu Dan of Pei marshal and Gu He chief clerk.
units.literal: At that time the Prince of Donghai, Chong, was Colonel of Changshui and chose his staff with care, appointing Liu Dan of Pei as marshal and Gu He as chief clerk.

units.zh: 永昌初，除司徒掾。
units.en: At the start of the Yongchang reign he received appointment as secretary to the Minister of Education.
units.literal: In the early Yongchang era he was appointed aide to the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 太甯初，王敦請為主簿，遷太子舍人、車騎參軍、護軍長史。
units.en: Early in Taining, Wang Dun took him on as chief clerk; he rose to gentleman-attendant at the heir’s palace, then adviser on the staff of the chariot-and-cavalry general and chief clerk to the Army Protector.
units.literal: In the early Taining era Wang Dun requested him as chief clerk; he was promoted to attendant of the heir apparent, army adviser to the chariot and cavalry general, and senior clerk to the Army Protector.

units.zh: 王導為揚州，請為別駕，所歷皆著稱。
units.en: When Wang Dao ran Yang Province he brought Gu He in as provincial aide; everywhere he served, people praised him.
units.literal: When Wang Dao governed Yang Province he invited him as Provincial Aide; in every post he earned acclaim.

units.zh: 遷散騎侍郎、尚書吏部。
units.en: He moved up to gentleman of the palace gate and served in the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman at the Palace Gate and Minister in the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 司空郗鑒請為長史，領晉陵太守。
units.en: Xi Jian, minister of works, asked him to serve as chief clerk while doubling as prefect of Jinling.
units.literal: Minister of Works Xi Jian requested him as senior clerk and concurrent Administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 咸康初，拜御史中丞，劾奏尚書左丞戴抗髒汙百萬，付法議罪，並免尚書傅玩、郎劉傭官，百僚憚之。
units.en: Early in Xiankang he became imperial censor and charged Assistant Minister of the Left Dai Kang with embezzling a million cash, sending the case to the courts; Minister Fu Wan and Gentleman Liu Yong were stripped of office as well. The bureaucracy trembled at him.
units.literal: In the early Xiankang era he was appointed Palace Assistant Censor and impeached the Left Assistant Minister Dai Kang for corruption involving a million in cash, handing him to the judiciary for sentencing; he also secured dismissal for Minister Fu Wan and Gentleman Liu Yong—the hundred officials all feared him.

units.zh: 遷侍中。
units.en: He was elevated to palace attendant.
units.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 初，中興東遷，舊章多闕，而冕旒飾以翡翠珊瑚及雜珠等。
units.en: After the court fled east, many ritual codes were lost; even the twelve strings of the imperial crown had been decked out with jadeite, coral, and assorted beads.
units.literal: Earlier, when the restoration moved the court eastward, old regulations were largely missing, and the king’s crown pendants were ornamented with jadeite, coral, and miscellaneous pearls.

units.zh: 和奏：「舊冕十有二旒，皆用玉珠，今用雜珠等，非禮。
units.en: Gu He submitted: “The classical crown carries twelve tassels of jade beads. Substituting mixed pearls breaks the rites.
units.literal: Gu He memorialized: “The ancient crown had twelve pendants, all of jade beads; now miscellaneous pearls are used—this is contrary to ritual.

units.zh: 若不能用玉，可用白旋珠。」
units.en: If true jade cannot be had, use white spinel pearls instead.”
units.literal: If jade cannot be used, white spinel pearls may be used.”

units.zh: 成帝於是始下太常改之。
units.en: Emperor Cheng then instructed the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to correct it.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng thereupon ordered the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to revise it.

units.zh: 先是，帝以保母周氏有阿保之勞，欲假其名號，內外皆奉詔。
units.en: Earlier the emperor wanted to give his wet nurse, Lady Zhou, an honorific rank for raising him, and the whole court was prepared to go along.
units.literal: Previously the emperor had wished to grant a title to his nurse, Lady Zhou, for her nurturing care; everyone inside and outside the court obeyed the edict.

units.zh: 和獨上疏以為「周保佑聖躬，不遺其勳，第舍供給擬于戚屬，恩澤所加已為過隆。
units.en: Gu He alone argued: “Lady Zhou had cared for the sovereign and already received ample reward—housing and allowances fit for family—and that further honors would overshoot decency.
units.literal: Gu He alone submitted a memorial arguing that “Lady Zhou had guarded the imperial person and her merit was not forgotten; her quarters and provisions already matched those of kin; the favor shown her was already excessive.

units.zh: 若假名號，記籍未見明比，惟漢靈帝以乳母趙嬈為平氏君，此末代之私恩，非先代之令典。
units.en: Granting her a formal title had no respectable precedent except Emperor Ling’s scandalous elevation of his nurse Zhao Rao—private indulgence from a fallen age, not a model worth following.
units.literal: If a title were granted, the records offered no clear parallel except Emperor Ling of Han elevating his wet nurse Zhao Rao as Lady of Ping—that was private favor from a degenerate age, not a standard from antiquity.

units.zh: 且君舉必書，將軌物垂則。
units.en: Besides, whatever a ruler does goes into the histories and becomes the pattern others must live by.
units.literal: Moreover every deed of a ruler is recorded; it is meant to set patterns for things and hand down models.

units.zh: 書而不法，後嗣何觀！」
units.en: Record something irregular, and what lesson does it teach those who come after!”
units.literal: If it is recorded yet not lawful, what will posterity think!”

units.zh: 帝從之。
units.en: The emperor agreed.
units.literal: The emperor accepted his view.

units.zh: 轉吏部尚書，頻徙領軍將軍、太常卿、國子祭酒。
units.en: He rotated into the Ministry of Personnel, then successively commanded the palace armies, headed the Chamberlain’s office, and served as libationer of the national university.
units.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, then moved several times to General Who Guards the Army, Chamberlain for Ceremonial, and Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 康帝即位，將祀南北郊，和議以為車駕宜親行。
units.en: Emperor Kang planned suburban sacrifices north and south; Gu He insisted the emperor should attend in person.
units.literal: When Emperor Kang ascended the throne and was about to sacrifice at the southern and northern suburban altars, Gu He argued that the imperial carriage ought to go in person.

units.zh: 帝從之，皆躬親行禮。
units.en: The emperor followed his advice and carried out every ritual himself.
units.literal: The emperor accepted it and personally performed the rites.

units.zh: 遷尚書僕射，以母老固辭，詔書敕喻，物聽暮出朝還，其見優遇如此。
units.en: Promoted to vice director of the secretariat, he begged off because his mother was elderly; the throne wrote to insist and let him go home at nightfall yet attend audiences at dawn—an extraordinary courtesy.
units.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat but firmly declined on account of his mother’s age; an edict urged him on and allowed him to leave court at dusk and return at dawn—such was the favor shown him.

units.zh: 尋朝議以端右之副不宜處外，更拜銀青光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。
units.en: Court opinion soon decided the vice premier ought not hold an outside post, so he was made grand master of the palace with silver and blue ribbon while remaining libationer of the academy.
units.literal: Soon court opinion held that the deputy of the chief minister should not serve outside; he was reassigned as Grand Master with Silver and Blue Ribbon and Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 頃之，母憂去職，居喪以孝聞。
units.en: When his mother died he resigned and earned a reputation for exemplary mourning.
units.literal: Before long he left office for mourning over his mother and was famed for filial conduct.

units.zh: 既練，衛將軍褚裒上疏薦和，起為尚書令，遣散騎郎喻旨。
units.en: After the zhuan rites, Chu Pou, general who guards the court, recommended him for director of the secretariat and the court dispatched a palace messenger with the summons.
units.literal: After the second-month ceremony, General Who Guards the Court Chu Pou memorialized to recommend Gu He and summon him as Director of the Imperial Secretariat; a gentleman of the palace gate was sent to convey the order.

units.zh: 和每見逼促，輒號咷慟絕，謂所親曰：「古人或有釋其憂服以祗王命，蓋以才足干時，故不得不體國徇義。
units.en: Each time officials pressured him, Gu He sobbed until he fainted and told his intimates, “Ancient worthies sometimes shed mourning to obey a summons when their abilities were indispensable—but I am less capable than most even in ordinary times.
units.literal: Whenever Gu He was pressed, he would wail until he lost consciousness and said to those close to him, “Men of old sometimes set aside mourning garb to answer the king’s command because their talent met the needs of the age and they could not but put the state before personal duty.

units.zh: 吾在常日猶不如人，況今中心荒亂，將何以補於萬分，只足以示輕忘孝道，貽素冠之義耳。」
units.en: Now my mind is in ruins—what good could I do? I would only advertise disdain for mourning and shame the ideal of the unadorned cap.”
units.literal: How much less now, when my heart is in chaos—how could I supply even a fraction of what is needed? I would only show contempt for filial piety and betray the meaning of the plain cap.”

units.zh: 帝又下詔曰：「百揆務殷，端右總要，而曠職經久，甚以悒然。
units.en: The emperor wrote again: “State business piles up and the director’s office is the hinge of government, yet it stands vacant—this weighs on me.
units.literal: The emperor issued another edict: “The myriad duties are pressing and the chief minister’s post is vital, yet it has long stood empty—I am deeply troubled.

units.zh: 昔先朝政道休明，中夏隆盛，山賈諸公皆釋服從時，不獲遂其情禮。
units.en: Under earlier reigns, when the realm prospered, even men like Shan Tao put aside mourning to serve—they could not cling to private grief alone.
units.literal: In former times, when government was enlightened and the Central Plain flourished, gentlemen such as Shan Tao still set aside mourning to follow the times and could not indulge private feeling.

units.zh: 況今日艱難百王之弊，尚書令禮已過祥練，豈得聽不赴急疾而遂罔極之情乎！」
units.en: Today’s troubles pile higher still; you have already passed the extended mourning stages—can we let you hide in endless sorrow while the realm waits?”
units.literal: How much more today amid the hardships and inherited ills of a hundred kings—the Director of the Secretariat has already passed the auspicious and practice periods—can he be allowed to heed boundless grief and ignore urgent need!”

units.zh: 和表疏十餘上，遂不起，服闋，然後視職。
units.en: Gu He answered with over ten memorials refusing to serve; he reported for duty only after the mourning term closed.
units.literal: Gu He submitted more than ten memorials and would not rise; only after mourning ended did he take office.

units.zh: 時南中郎將謝尚領宣城內史，收涇令陳幹殺之，有司以尚違法糾黜，詔原之。
units.en: Xie Shang, leader of the southern household guards and acting prefect of Xuancheng, seized and executed Jing county magistrate Chen Gan. Officials wanted him cashiered for breaking statute, but an edict let him off.
units.literal: At that time the General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Household, Xie Shang, concurrently administered Xuancheng interior commandery: he arrested and executed Magistrate Chen Gan of Jing. The authorities ruled that Shang had violated the law and should be dismissed; an edict pardoned him.

units.zh: 和重奏曰：「尚先劾奸髒罪，入甲戍赦，聽自首減死。
units.en: Gu He fired back: “Xie Shang first denounced Chen Gan’s graft; the matter was covered by the Jiaxu amnesty, which permitted voluntary surrender to avoid execution.
units.literal: Gu He submitted a further memorial: “Shang had earlier impeached Gan for corruption; the case fell under the Jiaxu amnesty, which allowed confession in exchange for commuting the death sentence.

units.zh: 而尚近表雲幹包藏奸猾，輒收行刑。
units.en: Now Xie Shang writes that Chen Gan was secretly malicious and therefore had to be arrested and killed.
units.literal: Yet Shang’s recent memorial claims Gan harbored treachery and so he seized and executed him.

units.zh: 幹事狀自郡，非犯軍戎，不由都督。
units.en: The case belonged to the civil administration—it was no battlefield offense and never crossed the regional commander’s desk.
units.literal: Gan’s affair arose from the commandery; it did not involve military crime and did not pass through the area commander.

units.zh: 案尚蒙親賢之舉，荷文武之任，不能為國惜體，平心聽斷，內挾小憾，肆其威虐，遠近怪愕，莫不解體。
units.en: Xie Shang was picked as a trusted elite with both civil and martial duty, yet he indulged a private spite and threw his weight around instead of protecting the law’s dignity; officials everywhere were dumbfounded and lost faith in him.
units.literal: Consider: Shang enjoys selection as a trusted worthy and bears civil and military responsibility; he could not safeguard the dignity of the state or judge impartially—instead he nursed a petty grudge and wantonly abused his power. Near and far were astonished; none failed to lose confidence.

units.zh: 尚忝外屬，宥之有典，至於下吏，宜正刑辟。」
units.en: Because he is imperial in-law, mercy may have precedent—but junior officers who abuse authority deserve the full penalty.”
units.literal: Shang, though related to the empress dowager’s kin, may be forgiven under precedent; as for subordinate clerks, proper punishment should be applied.”

units.zh: 尚，皇太后舅，故寢其奏。
units.en: Xie Shang was the empress dowager’s uncle, so the throne quietly buried Gu He’s protest.
units.literal: Shang was the empress dowager’s uncle, so the memorial was shelved.

units.zh: 時汝南王統、江夏公衛崇並為庶母制服三年，和乃奏曰：「禮所以軌物成教，故有國家者莫不崇正明本，以一其統，斯人倫之紀，不二之道也。
units.en: When Prince Tong of Runan and Duke Wei Chong of Jiangxia both wore three-year mourning for foster mothers, Gu He argued: “Rites govern behavior and teaching; every state affirms one legitimate lineage. That principle admits no split allegiance.
units.literal: At that time the Prince of Runan, Tong, and Duke of Jiangxia, Wei Chong, both observed three years’ mourning for a concubine mother. Gu He therefore memorialized: “Ritual exists to regulate conduct and complete instruction; therefore those who possess a state none fail to honor the correct root and unify the system—this is the norm of human relations and the single path that admits no doubling.

units.zh: 為人後者，降其所出，奪天屬之性，顯至公之義，降殺節文，著于周典。
units.en: Adopted heirs downgrade birth parents to serve the main line—the Zhou rituals spell out the gradations.
units.literal: Those who become heirs to another line demote their birth parents, strip natural affection in favor of supreme impartiality, and the graduated rules are set forth in the Zhou canon.

units.zh: 案汝南王統為庶母居廬服重，江夏公衛崇本由疏屬，開國之緒，近喪所生，復行重制，違冒禮度，肆其私情。
units.en: Prince Tong keeps full mourning for a concubine; Duke Wei, a distant cadet ennobled only by the founding ancestor, buries his natural mother and then insists on the heaviest rites—flouting protocol for private sentiment.
units.literal: Consider: the Prince of Runan wears deep mourning in a hut for a concubine mother; Duke Wei Chong, born from a distant branch, owes his noble fief to the founding line, yet having lately buried his birth mother he again observes heavy mourning—violating ritual bounds and indulging private feeling.

units.zh: 閭閻許其過厚，談者莫以為非，則政道陵遲由乎禮廢，憲章頹替始于容違。
units.en: If neighbors call it devotion and no one objects, governance slides because rites erode and law frays where exceptions multiply.
units.literal: If commoners praise their excessive devotion and critics say nothing is wrong, then government declines because ritual collapses, and statutes crumble because indulgence is tolerated.

units.zh: 若弗糾正，無以齊物。
units.en: Unless we correct this, we cannot hold everyone to one standard.
units.literal: If this is not corrected, there is no way to standardize conduct.

units.zh: 皆可下太常奪服。
units.en: Send them all to the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to remove the improper mourning.
units.literal: All may be ordered through the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to strip the mourning garb.

units.zh: 若不祗王命，應加貶黜。」
units.en: Anyone who defies the decree should be degraded.”
units.literal: If they disobey the royal command, demotion should be added.”

units.zh: 詔從之。
units.en: The court approved.
units.literal: An edict followed his advice.

units.zh: 和居任多所獻納，雖權臣不苟阿撓。
units.en: Throughout his tenure he spoke plainly to the throne and refused to truckle to mighty favorites.
units.literal: In office Gu He offered many remonstrances and recommendations; even toward powerful ministers he would not cringe or yield.

units.zh: 永和七年，以疾篤辭位，拜左光祿大夫、儀同三司，加散騎常侍，尚書令如故。
units.en: In the seventh year of Yonghe, grave illness forced Gu He to yield his offices; the court still named him grand master of the left with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, added gentleman at the palace gate, and allowed him to remain director of the secretariat.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Yonghe, because Gu He's illness was grave he resigned office; he was appointed Grand Master of the Left, Unequaled in Honor, concurrently Gentleman at the Palace Gate, while retaining his post as Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 其年卒，年六十四。
units.en: He died the same year at sixty-four.
units.literal: That same year he died, aged sixty-four.

units.zh: 追贈侍中、司空，諡曰穆。
units.en: He was posthumously named palace attendant and minister of works with the epithet Mu, meaning Solemn.
units.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; his posthumous name was Mu.

units.zh: 子淳，歷尚書吏部郎、給事黃門侍郎、左衛將軍。
units.en: His son Gu Chun rose through personnel posts, the yellow-gate palace corps, and command of the left guard.
units.literal: His son Chun served as Gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel, Gentleman for Palace Presentation at the Yellow Gate, and General Who Guards the Left.

units.zh: 袁瑰
units.en: Yuan Gui
units.literal: Yuan Gui

units.zh: 袁瑰，字山甫，陳郡陽夏人，魏郎中令渙之曾孫也。
units.en: Yuan Gui, courtesy Shanfu, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery and traced his descent from Yuan Huan, minister of gentlemen under Wei.
units.literal: Yuan Gui, courtesy name Shanfu, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery and great-grandson of Yuan Huan, who had been Director of Gentlemen under Wei.

units.zh: 祖、父並早卒。
units.en: Both his grandfather and father died early.
units.literal: His grandfather and father both died young.

units.zh: 瑰與弟猷欲奉母避亂，求為江淮間縣，拜呂令，轉江都，因南渡。
units.en: He and his brother You sought a riverside county post so they could move their mother out of chaos—first magistrate of Lü, then Jiangdu—and crossed south with her.
units.literal: Gui and his younger brother You wished to escort their mother away from turmoil and sought appointment to a county between the Yangzi and Huai; he was appointed magistrate of Lü, then transferred to Jiangdu, and thus crossed south.

units.zh: 元帝以為丹陽令。
units.en: Emperor Yuan named him prefect of Danyang.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him magistrate of Danyang.

units.zh: 中興建，拜奉朝請，遷治書御史。
units.en: After the eastern court was established he became court presenter and then imperial secretary.
units.literal: When the restoration was founded he was appointed Court Presenter and promoted to palace secretary.

units.zh: 時東海王越屍既為石勒所焚，妃裴氏求招魂葬越，朝廷疑之。
units.en: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, had already had his corpse burned by Shi Le; his consort Lady Pei asked to bury a soul-summoning garment in lieu of remains, and ministers hesitated.
units.literal: At that time the Prince of Donghai, Yue, had already had his corpse burned by Shi Le; his consort Lady Pei sought to summon his soul for burial, and the court was uncertain.

units.zh: 瑰與博士傅純議，以為招魂葬是謂埋神，不可從也。
units.en: Yuan Gui and scholar Fu Chun argued that “summoning the soul” amounted to burying a ghost-soul and must be refused.
units.literal: Gui debated with Erudite Fu Chun and argued that soul-summoning burial meant burying the spirit and could not be permitted.

units.zh: 帝然之，雖許裴氏招魂葬越，遂下詔禁之。
units.en: The emperor accepted in principle yet let Lady Pei bury Prince Yue’s effigy, then banned the custom by edict.
units.literal: The emperor agreed; although he allowed Lady Pei’s soul burial for Yue, he then issued an edict forbidding the practice.

units.zh: 尋除廬江太守。
units.en: Shortly afterward he became prefect of Lujiang.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Lujiang.

units.zh: 大將軍王敦引為諮議參軍。
units.en: Wang Dun took him on as consulting adviser.
units.literal: Grand General Wang Dun brought him in as adviser on his staff.

units.zh: 俄為臨川太守。
units.en: He soon transferred to Linchuan prefect.
units.literal: Before long he was Administrator of Linchuan.

units.zh: 敦平，為鎮南將軍陶侃軍司。
units.en: Once Wang Dun was defeated, Yuan Gui became army marshal on Tao Kan’s staff in the southern command.
units.literal: After Dun was crushed he served as army marshal to General Who Guards the South Tao Kan.

units.zh: 尋自解還都，游於會稽。
units.en: He soon resigned and came back to Jiankang, then wandered in Kuaiji.
units.literal: Soon he resigned on his own initiative and returned to the capital, then traveled in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 蘇峻之難，與王舒共起義軍，以功封長合鄉侯，征補散騎常侍，徙大司農尋除國子祭酒。
units.en: When Su Jun rebelled he mustered forces with Wang Shu, earned a village marquisate at Changhe, returned to court as gentleman at the palace gate, moved to minister of agriculture, and shortly became libationer of the academy.
units.literal: During Su Jun’s rebellion he raised troops with Wang Shu; for merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changhe, summoned as Gentleman at the Palace Gate, transferred to Minister of Agriculture, and soon appointed Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

units.zh: 頃之，加散騎常侍。
units.en: He soon picked up a concurrent post as gentleman at the palace gate.
units.literal: Before long he was additionally Gentleman at the Palace Gate.

units.zh: 于時喪亂之後，禮教陵遲，瑰上疏曰：
units.en: With the realm broken and etiquette in ruins, Yuan Gui addressed the throne:
units.literal: At that time, after deaths and turmoil, ritual teaching had declined; Gui submitted a memorial saying:

units.zh: 疏奏，成帝從之。
units.en: Emperor Cheng approved his memorial.
units.literal: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Cheng accepted it.

units.zh: 國學之興，自瑰始也。
units.en: The national university owed its revival to Yuan Gui.
units.literal: The revival of the national academy began with Gui.

units.zh: 以年在懸車，上疏告老，尋卒，追贈光祿大夫，諡曰恭。
units.en: Past the conventional retirement age he asked leave to retire, died soon after, and received posthumous honors as grand master of brilliant splendor with the canonizing epithet Gong.
units.literal: Because his years had reached the age for retiring (“suspended carriage”), he memorialized to retire; soon afterward he died and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor with the posthumous name Gong.

units.zh: 子喬嗣。
units.en: His son Yuan Qiao succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Qiao inherited.

units.zh: 子喬
units.en: Yuan Qiao.
units.literal: Qiao.

units.zh: 子喬
units.en: Yuan Qiao
units.literal: Son Qiao

units.zh: 喬字彥叔。
units.en: Yuan Qiao’s courtesy name was Yanshu.
units.literal: Qiao’s courtesy name was Yanshu.

units.zh: 初拜佐著作郎。
units.en: He began as assistant editor in the institute.
units.literal: At first he was appointed editorial aide.

units.zh: 輔國將軍桓溫請為司馬，除司徒左西屬，不就，拜尚書郎。
units.en: Huan Wen tried to hire him as marshal; the court named him western aide under the minister of education—he refused—and then gentleman of the secretariat.
units.literal: General Who Supports the State Huan Wen requested him as marshal; he was appointed western aide on the left of the Minister of Education but declined; he was appointed Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 桓溫鎮京口，復引為司馬，領廣陵相。
units.en: Huan Wen, stationed at Jingkou, recalled Yuan Qiao as his marshal and put him in charge of Guangling as well.
units.literal: When Huan Wen garrisoned Jingkou he again brought Yuan Qiao in as marshal and concurrent Administrator of Guangling.

units.zh: 初，喬與褚裒友善，及康獻皇后臨朝，喬與裒書曰：「皇太后踐登正阼，臨御皇朝，將軍之于國，外姓之太上皇也。
units.en: Yuan Qiao had long been close to Chu Pou. Once Empress Dowager Kangxian began regency, he wrote: “The queen mother sits on the proper throne and governs the realm—you are to this court what a paramount father-in-law would be to an outsider clan.
units.literal: Earlier Qiao had been friendly with Chu Pou. When Empress Dowager Kangxian held court, Qiao wrote to Pou: “The empress dowager has ascended the legitimate throne and rules the dynasty; for you, General, in relation to the state, you are like a senior emperor by marriage though not of the imperial surname.

units.zh: 至於皇子近屬，咸有揖讓之禮，而況策名人臣，而交媟人父，天性攸尊，亦宜體國而重矣。
units.en: Even imperial kin still observe deference in public—how much more a minister listed in the roster who would bandy intimacies with another man’s father? Natural obligations of respect exist; you should put the polity first.
units.literal: Even imperial princes and close kin observe yielding courtesy—how much more one who bears ministerial rank on the roster yet behaves toward another man’s father with improper familiarity? Nature sets whom we must honor; you too should weigh the state above private feeling.

units.zh: 故友之好，請於此辭。
units.en: So I must end our former friendship at this point.
units.literal: Therefore I ask to end our old friendship here.

units.zh: 染絲之變，墨翟致懷，岐路之感，楊硃興歎，況于將軍游處少長，雖世譽先後而臭味同歸也。
units.en: Mozi mourned how silk changes color in the dye; Yang Zhu wept at life’s diverging roads—so too for us, friends since youth: fame may come sooner or later, but we breathed the same air.
units.literal: The dyeing of silk moved Mozi; the fork in the road made Yang Zhu sigh—how much more we who have grown up together: though the world praised us in different order, our temperaments belong to the same track.

units.zh: 平昔之交，與禮數而降，箕踞之歎，隨時事而替，雖欲虛詠濠肆，脫落儀制，其能得乎！
units.en: Courtesy now narrows what old camaraderie allowed; the reproof for sprawling discourtesy shifts with the times—there is no going back to abstract chatter about Zhuangzi’s Hao-river debates and shedding ritual.
units.literal: Plain friendship must yield to ritual gradations; the lounging reproach changes with events—how could we still babble of Zhuangzi’s riverside freedom and cast off formalities?

units.zh: 來物無停，變化遷代，豈惟寸晷，事亦有之。
units.en: Nothing stays still; times turn over faster than a shadow—circumstances move too.
units.literal: Coming things never pause; change and succession roll on—not only in brief moments; affairs do the same.

units.zh: 夫禦器者神，制衆以約，願將軍貽情無事，以理勝為任，親杖賢達，以納善為大。
units.en: The pilot must be nimble; governing crowds demands simplicity—please quiet personal feeling while things are still, make order your burden, draw near to the wise, and prize sound advice above all.
units.literal: He who steers the vessel must be spirit-like; he who rules the many must keep restraint. I hope you will set emotion aside while affairs are calm, take defeating chaos as your task, lean on worthy men, and make welcoming good counsel your chief aim.

units.zh: 執筆惆悵，不能自盡。」
units.en: Pen in hand, I am heavy-hearted and cannot say all I mean.”
units.literal: Holding the brush I am melancholy and cannot fully express myself.”

units.zh: 論者以為得禮。
units.en: Opinion held that he had struck the proper ritual note.
units.literal: Commentators held that he had understood ritual propriety.

units.zh: 遷安西諮議參軍、長沙相，不拜。
units.en: They moved him to adviser under the general pacifying the west and offered him Changsha—he declined both.
units.literal: He was transferred to adviser on the staff of the General Who Pacifies the West and Chancellor of Changsha but did not take office.

units.zh: 尋督沔中諸戍江夏隨義陽三郡軍事、建武將軍、江夏相。
units.en: He then commanded Han River defenses plus Jiangxia, Sui, and Yiyang as General Who Establishes Might and prefect of Jiangxia.
units.literal: Soon he supervised military affairs of the garrisons along the Han and the three commanderies Jiangxia, Sui, and Yiyang, served as General Who Establishes Might, and was Chancellor of Jiangxia.

units.zh: 時桓溫謀伐蜀，衆以為不可，喬勸溫曰：「夫經略大事，故非常情所具，智者了于胸心，然後舉無遺算耳。
units.en: When Huan Wen aimed at Shu, court opinion scoffed. Yuan Qiao told him, “Great campaigns exceed common sense—only when a strategist has done the math in silence does the plan hold.
units.literal: At that time Huan Wen planned to attack Shu; most thought it impossible. Qiao urged Wen: “Grand strategy is not what ordinary minds grasp—only after a wise man has settled it in his breast does an undertaking leave nothing unplanned.

units.zh: 今天下之難，二寇而已。
units.en: The empire today faces just two enemies.
units.literal: The peril facing the realm today is only two bandits.

units.zh: 蜀雖險固，方胡為弱，將欲除之，先從易者。
units.en: Shu is steep but weaker than the northern tribes—cut the weak link first.
units.literal: Shu is rugged, but compared with the Hu it is the weaker; if you intend to eliminate them, begin with the easier.

units.zh: 今溯流萬里，經歷天險，彼或有備，不必可克。
units.en: A river assault ten thousand li upstream runs every natural hazard—the enemy may be ready, so success is no certainty.
units.literal: Attacking upriver ten thousand li through heaven’s narrows, they may be prepared and victory is not assured.

units.zh: 然蜀人自以鬥絕一方，恃其完固，不修攻戰之具，若以精卒一萬，輕軍速進，比彼聞之，我已入其險要，李勢君臣不過自力一戰，擒之必矣。
units.en: Still, Shu rests smug behind its walls and lets its arms rust—strike with ten thousand elites before rumor catches up, seize the narrows, and Li Shi’s regime will manage one frantic fight at best; victory follows.
units.literal: Yet the Shu people pride themselves on isolation, trust their fortifications, and neglect weapons; if with ten thousand picked troops you march fast and light, by the time word reaches them you will already hold the choke points—Li Shi’s court can manage only one desperate battle; capture is certain.

units.zh: 論者恐大軍既西，胡必窺覦，此又似是而非。
units.en: Critics warn that marching west invites Hu raids—it sounds sensible but is not.
units.literal: Critics fear that once the main army goes west the Hu will spy an opening—this sounds plausible yet is wrong.

units.zh: 何者？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 胡聞萬里片征伐，以為內有重備，必不敢動。
units.en: Northern tribes hearing of an expedition far away conclude the interior is heavily guarded and hesitate to move.
units.literal: When the Hu hear that a campaign ten thousand li away is underway, they assume heavy interior defenses and will not dare stir.

units.zh: 縱復越逸江渚，諸軍足以守境，此無憂矣。
units.en: Should raiders ford the Yangzi anyway, frontier armies can contain them—there is little to fear.
units.literal: Even if raiders slip across the Yangzi, our garrisons suffice to hold the frontier—there is no worry.

units.zh: 蜀土富實，號稱天府，昔諸葛武侯欲以抗衡中國。
units.en: Shu is fertile—Zhuge Liang once meant to use it to challenge the heartland.
units.literal: Shu’s soil is rich and famed as heaven’s storehouse; once Zhuge Liang meant to rival the Central Plain.

units.zh: 今誠不能為害，然勢據上流，易為寇盜。
units.en: It cannot hurt us much now, yet perched upstream it invites marauders.
units.literal: Today it truly cannot harm us, yet sitting upstream it easily breeds banditry.

units.zh: 若襲而取之者，有其人衆，此國之大利也。」
units.en: Taking it yields manpower—a major prize for the state.”
units.literal: If we seize it we gain its population—that is the realm’s great profit.”

units.zh: 溫從之，使喬以江夏相領二千人為軍鋒。
units.en: Huan Wen agreed and gave Yuan Qiao two thousand Jiangxia troops as vanguard.
units.literal: Wen accepted this and ordered Qiao, as Chancellor of Jiangxia, to lead two thousand men as the army’s spearhead.

units.zh: 師次彭模，去賊已近，議者欲兩道並進，以分賊勢。
units.en: They camped at Pengmo with the foe close by; staff urged a two-pronged advance to divide Shu forces.
units.literal: The army halted at Pengmo; the enemy was near. Advisers wished to advance along two routes to split enemy strength.

units.zh: 喬曰：「今深入萬里，置之死地，士無反顧之心，所謂人自為戰者也。
units.en: Yuan Qiao replied, “We are ten thousand li deep on fatal terrain—soldiers fight as if their lives depend on each stroke.
units.literal: Qiao said: “Now we have plunged ten thousand li and placed the army on deadly ground; the men have no thought of turning back—each fights as if for himself.

units.zh: 今分為兩軍，軍力不一，萬一偏敗，則大事去矣。
units.en: Split the force and uneven odds mean one defeat loses everything.
units.literal: If we split into two armies with uneven strength, should one wing fail the whole enterprise is lost.

units.zh: 不如全軍而進，棄去釜甑，齎三日糧，勝可必矣。」
units.en: Better drive forward intact, smash the cauldrons, march with three days’ rations—then we cannot lose.”
units.literal: Better advance with the whole army, cast aside cooking pots, carry three days’ grain—then victory is assured.

units.zh: 溫以為然，即一時俱進。
units.en: Huan Wen concurred and pushed everyone forward together.
units.literal: Wen agreed and advanced all at once.

units.zh: 去成都十里，與賊大戰，前鋒失利，喬軍亦退，矢及馬首，左右失色。
units.en: Ten li short of Chengdu the great clash came—the van broke, Yuan Qiao’s men wavered, bolts whipped his mount’s mane, and aides turned pale.
units.literal: Ten li from Chengdu they fought a great battle; the vanguard faltered, Qiao’s line fell back, arrows reached his horse’s head, and his attendants blanched.

units.zh: 喬因麾而進，聲氣愈厲，遂大破之，長驅至成都。
units.en: Yuan Qiao signaled the advance, shouted louder, shattered the Shu host, and raced to Chengdu.
units.literal: Qiao waved the army onward; his voice grew fiercer; they routed the enemy and drove straight to Chengdu.

units.zh: 李勢既降，勢將鄧定、隗文以其屬反，衆各萬餘。
units.en: Once Li Shi yielded, generals Deng Ding and Kui Wen revolted with ten thousand men apiece.
units.literal: After Li Shi surrendered, his generals Deng Ding and Kui Wen rebelled with their commands, each over ten thousand strong.

units.zh: 溫自擊定，喬擊文，破之。
units.en: Huan Wen took Deng Ding himself; Yuan Qiao crushed Kui Wen.
units.literal: Wen personally attacked Ding while Qiao attacked Wen and defeated them.

units.zh: 進號龍驤將軍，封湘西伯。
units.en: He was promoted to dragon-soaring general and made baron of Xiangxi.
units.literal: Qiao’s rank rose to General Who Soars like the Dragon; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xiangxi.

units.zh: 尋卒，年三十六，溫甚悼惜之。
units.en: He died soon after at thirty-six; Huan Wen grieved bitterly.
units.literal: Soon he died at age thirty-six; Wen deeply mourned him.

units.zh: 追贈益州刺史，諡曰簡。
units.en: The court posthumously named him inspector of Yi with the epithet Jian, meaning Simple.
units.literal: Posthumously he was honored as Inspector of Yi Province with the posthumous name Jian.

units.zh: 喬博學有文才，注《論語》及《詩》，並諸文筆皆行於世。
units.en: Yuan Qiao was learned and wrote well—his glosses on the Analects and the Odes plus his essays stayed in circulation.
units.literal: Qiao was broadly learned and literary; he annotated the Analects and the Odes, and his essays circulated widely.

units.zh: 子方平嗣，亦以軌素自立，辟大司馬掾，歷義興、琅邪太守。
units.en: His son Fangping succeeded, kept a sober household, joined the grand marshal’s staff, and governed Yixing and Langye.
units.literal: His son Fangping inherited; he too upheld plain integrity, was summoned as aide to the grand marshal, and served as Administrator of Yixing and Langye.

units.zh: 卒，子山松嗣。
units.en: On his death his son Shansong inherited the line.
units.literal: When he died, his son Shansong inherited.

units.zh: 喬孫山松
units.en: Yuan Shansong, Qiao’s grandson
units.literal: Grandson Shansong

units.zh: 喬孫山松
units.en: Yuan Shansong
units.literal: Grandson Shansong

units.zh: 山松少有才名，博學有文章，著《後漢書》百篇。
units.en: Shansong was celebrated young—learned, prolific, author of a hundred-chapter Later Han history.
units.literal: Shansong in youth had a talented name; he was learned and wrote well, composing a hundred-chapter Later Han.

units.zh: 衿情秀遠，善音樂。
units.en: He carried an aloof grace and loved music.
units.literal: His temperament was refined and remote; he excelled at music.

units.zh: 舊歌有《行路難》曲，辭頗疏質，山松好之，乃文其辭句，婉其節制，每因酣醉縱歌之。
units.en: The old song “Hard Road” had crude words; Shansong refined the verse and meter, then belted it whenever wine flowed.
units.literal: An old ballad had the tune “Hard Road”; its words were rough. Shansong loved it, polished the lyrics, smoothed the rhythm, and whenever drunk would sing it wildly.

units.zh: 聽者莫不流涕。
units.en: Listeners wept every time.
units.literal: Listeners invariably wept.

units.zh: 初羊曇善唱樂，桓伊能輓歌，及山松《行路難》繼之，時人謂之「三絕」。
units.en: Yang Tan sang beautifully, Huan Yi mastered dirges, then Shansong’s “Hard Road”—contemporaries dubbed them the three incomparables.
units.literal: Once Yang Tan sang well and Huan Yi could sing laments; Shansong’s “Hard Road” followed—people of the time called them the “three unmatched talents.”

units.zh: 時張湛好於齋前種松柏，而山松每出遊，好令左右作輓歌，人謂「湛屋下陳屍，山松道上行殯。」
units.en: Zhang Zhan grew pines and cypress by his study; Shansong paraded with hired mourners—wags said, “Zhan stacks corpses at home while Shansong holds street funerals.”
units.literal: Zhang Zhan liked planting pines and cypress before his study; whenever Shansong went out he had attendants perform lambsongs—people said “Corpses laid out under Zhan’s roof; funeral processions march wherever Shansong rides.”

units.zh: 山松歷顯位，為吳郡太守。
units.en: He climbed to high office and governed Wu commandery.
units.literal: Shansong rose to eminent posts and became Administrator of Wu Commandery.

units.zh: 孫恩作亂，山松守滬瀆，城陷被害。
units.en: Sun En’s revolt caught him defending Hudu—the city fell and he died.
units.literal: When Sun En rebelled, Shansong defended Hudu; the city fell and he was killed.

units.zh: 瑰弟猷
units.en: Yuan You, Gui’s younger brother.
units.literal: Gui’s younger brother You.

units.zh: 瑰弟猷
units.en: Yuan You.
units.literal: Gui’s younger brother You.

units.zh: 猷字申甫，少與瑰齊名。
units.en: You bore the courtesy name Shenfu and in youth was as celebrated as Gui.
units.literal: You, courtesy name Shenfu, in youth shared Gui’s reputation.

units.zh: 代瑰為呂令，復相繼為江都，由是俱渡江。
units.en: He followed Gui as prefect of Lü, then Jiangdu in turn, and crossed south with him.
units.literal: He succeeded Gui as magistrate of Lü and afterward likewise served Jiangdu; thus both crossed the Yangzi.

units.zh: 瑰為丹陽，猷為武康，兄弟列宰名邑，論者美之。
units.en: While Gui ran Danyang, You governed Wukang—brothers holding celebrated seats together won admiration.
units.literal: Gui governed Danyang and You Wukang; as brothers they administered famed counties together—critics praised them.

units.zh: 歷位侍中、衛尉卿。
units.en: He advanced to palace attendant and minister of the palace guard.
units.literal: He rose through Palace Attendant and Chamberlain of the Guards.

units.zh: 猷孫宏，見《文苑傳》。
units.en: His grandson Yuan Hong is treated in the Literary Men section.
units.literal: You’s grandson Hong appears in the “Literary Men” biography.

units.zh: 從祖準
units.en: Yuan Zhun, collateral great-uncle.
units.literal: Collateral ancestor Zhun.

units.zh: 從祖準
units.en: Yuan Zhun.
units.literal: Collateral ancestor Zhun.

units.zh: 準字孝尼，以儒學知名，注《喪服經》。
units.en: Zhun, courtesy Xiaoni, earned renown as a classicist and wrote a commentary on mourning grades.
units.literal: Zhun, courtesy name Xiaoni, was famed for Confucian scholarship and annotated the Scripture on Mourning Garb.

units.zh: 官至給事中。
units.en: He capped his career as palace aide.
units.literal: His highest office was palace aide.

units.zh: 準子沖，字景玄，光祿勳。
units.en: His son Chong, courtesy Jingxuan, rose to minister of the imperial household.
units.literal: Zhun’s son Chong, courtesy name Jingxuan, served as Minister of Brilliant Splendor.

units.zh: 沖子耽。
units.en: Chong’s heir was Dan.
units.literal: Chong’s son Dan.

units.zh: 準孫耽
units.en: Yuan Dan, grandson of Zhun.
units.literal: Zhun’s grandson Dan.

units.zh: 準孫耽
units.en: Yuan Dan.
units.literal: Zhun’s grandson Dan.

units.zh: 耽字彥道，少有才氣，倜儻不羈，為士類所稱。
units.en: Dan, courtesy Yandao, had flair and swagger from youth and impressed the elite.
units.literal: Dan, courtesy name Yandao, showed youthful brilliance and unruly dash and won praise among gentlemen.

units.zh: 桓溫少時游於博徒，資產俱盡，尚有負進，思自振之方，莫知所出，欲求濟於耽，而耽在艱，試以告焉。
units.en: In youth Huan Wen gambled away his fortune and still owed money; desperate for rescue yet unsure how, he approached Dan—who was observing mourning—but tested the waters anyway.
units.literal: When Huan Wen was young he gambled until his assets were gone yet still owed debts; he sought a way to recover but knew none and wished to ask Dan for aid—Dan was in mourning but Wen tentatively told him.

units.zh: 耽略無難色，遂變服懷布帽，隨溫與債主戲。
units.en: Dan agreed without hesitation—changed clothes, hid a cloth cap under his jacket, and joined Huan Wen at the creditor’s table.
units.literal: Dan showed no reluctance; he changed clothes, tucked a cloth cap under his arm, and followed Wen to game with the creditor.

units.zh: 耽素有藝名，債者聞之而不相識，謂之曰：「卿當不辦作袁彥道也。」
units.en: Dan was legendary at dice; the creditor had heard the name but did not know his face and sneered, “You cannot possibly be Yuan Yandao.”
units.literal: Dan had long been famed for gaming skill; the creditor heard but did not recognize him and said, “You surely cannot play the part of Yuan Yandao.”

units.zh: 遂就局十萬一擲，直上百萬。
units.en: They opened play at a hundred thousand cash per cast—stakes shot toward a million.
units.literal: They then joined the game with one hundred thousand wagered per throw, climbing straight to a million.

units.zh: 耽投馬絕叫，探布帽擲地，曰：「竟識袁彥道不？」
units.en: Dan slammed his pieces down, hurled the cap to the floor, and roared, “Still doubt Yuan Yandao?”
units.literal: Dan cast the horses with a shout, pulled out the cloth cap and threw it down, saying, “Do you recognize Yuan Yandao now?”

units.zh: 其通脫若此。
units.en: Such was his swaggering nerve.
units.literal: His unconventionality was such as this.

units.zh: 蘇峻之役，王導引為參軍，隨導在石頭。
units.en: In Su Jun’s coup Wang Dao enlisted him as adviser, and he accompanied Dao at Stone fortress.
units.literal: During Su Jun’s rising Wang Dao brought him in as army adviser and followed Dao at Stone Citadel.

units.zh: 初，路永、匡術、寧等皆峻心腹，聞祖約奔敗，懼事不立，迭說峻誅大臣。
units.en: Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, Ning, and company had been Su Jun’s inner circle; when Zu Yue collapsed they feared the plot would unravel and pressed Su Jun to purge senior ministers.
units.literal: Earlier Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, Ning, and others had all been Su Jun’s trusted men; hearing Zu Yue had fled in defeat they feared the venture would fail and urged Jun repeatedly to execute great ministers.

units.zh: 峻既不納，永等慮必敗，陰結於導。
units.en: Su Jun refused; Yong’s faction foresaw doom and secretly negotiated with Wang Dao.
units.literal: Jun would not listen; Yong and company anticipated certain defeat and secretly allied with Dao.

units.zh: 導使耽潛說路永，使歸順。
units.en: Wang Dao had Dan approach Lu Yong quietly to defect.
units.literal: Dao sent Dan secretly to persuade Yong to surrender.

units.zh: 峻平，封秭歸男，拜建威將軍、曆陽太守。
units.en: When Su Jun fell, Dan earned the Zigui barony, generalship who establishes might, and Liyang prefect.
units.literal: After Jun was crushed Dan was enfeoffed as Baron of Zigui, appointed General Who Establishes Might, and Administrator of Liyang.

units.zh: 咸康初，石季龍游騎十餘匹至曆陽，耽上列不言騎少。
units.en: Early in Xiankang a handful of Shi Hu’s scouts appeared at Liyang; Dan’s report omitted how tiny the enemy band was.
units.literal: In the early Xiankang era Shi Jilong’s scouting riders—little more than a dozen horses—reached Liyang; Dan’s memorial listed them without mentioning how few they were.

units.zh: 時胡寇強盛，朝野危懼，王導以宰輔之重請自討之。
units.en: Northern pressure terrified everyone; chief minister Wang Dao volunteered to lead the response.
units.literal: At that time Hu raiders were strong and court and countryside trembled; Wang Dao in his weight as chief minister requested permission to campaign personally.

units.zh: 既而賊騎不多，又已退散，導止不行。
units.en: Soon there proved to be almost no raiders—they had melted away—so Wang Dao stayed home.
units.literal: Presently it proved there were few enemy riders and they had dispersed; Dao halted and did not go.

units.zh: 朝廷以耽失於輕妄，黜之。
units.en: The court cashiered Dan for reckless alarmism.
units.literal: The court deemed Dan rash and reckless and dismissed him.

units.zh: 尋復為導從事中郎，方加大任，會卒，時年二十五。
units.en: He returned as Wang Dao’s senior attendant on the verge of promotion but died at twenty-five.
units.literal: Soon he again served Dao as attendant gentleman-in-chief; high office was about to come when he died at age twenty-five.

units.zh: 子質。
units.en: His son was Zhi.
units.literal: Son Zhi.

units.zh: 耽子質
units.en: Yuan Zhi, Dan’s son.
units.literal: Dan’s son Zhi.

units.zh: 耽子質
units.en: Yuan Zhi.
units.literal: Dan’s son Zhi.

units.zh: 質字道和。
units.en: Zhi bore the courtesy name Daohe.
units.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Daohe.

units.zh: 自渙至質五世，並以道素繼業，惟其父耽以雄豪著。
units.en: Five generations from Yuan Huan through Zhi maintained sober virtue—only Dan stood out for swagger.
units.literal: From Huan down to Zhi for five generations all upheld plain moral continuity; only his father Dan was famed for brash heroism.

units.zh: 及質又以孝行稱。
units.en: Zhi himself earned renown for filial devotion.
units.literal: When it came to Zhi he was also praised for filial conduct.

units.zh: 官歷琅邪內史、東陽太守。
units.en: He governed Langye interior commandery and Dongyang prefecture.
units.literal: He served as Interior Minister of Langye and Administrator of Dongyang.

units.zh: 質子湛。
units.en: His heir was Zhan.
units.literal: Zhi’s son Zhan.

units.zh: 質子湛
units.en: Yuan Zhan, Zhi’s son.
units.literal: Zhi’s son Zhan.

units.zh: 質子湛
units.en: Yuan Zhan.
units.literal: Zhi’s son Zhan.

units.zh: 湛字士深。
units.en: Zhan used the courtesy name Shishen.
units.literal: Zhan, courtesy name Shishen.

units.zh: 少有操植，以沖粹自立，而無文華，故不為流俗所重。
units.en: Even young he cultivated restraint and sober virtue rather than polish, so fashionable circles overlooked him.
units.literal: From youth he held moral discipline and cultivated quiet purity without literary ornament, so vulgar taste did not esteem him.

units.zh: 時謝混為僕射，范泰贈湛及混詩云：「亦有後出雋，離群頗騫翥。」
units.en: While Xie Hun served as vice director Fan Tai gifted them verse praising “later luminaries who rise above the herd.”
units.literal: When Xie Hun was vice director Fan Tai presented Zhan and Hun a poem saying, “There are also late-coming talents who soar apart from the flock.”

units.zh: 湛恨而不答。
units.en: Zhan took offense and stayed silent.
units.literal: Zhan resented it and did not answer.

units.zh: 自中書令為僕射、左光祿大夫、晉甯男，卒於官。
units.en: He moved from palace director to vice director, grand master of the left, and baron of Jinning—dying in harness.
units.literal: From Palace Commandant he became vice director, Grand Master of the Left, and Baron of Jinning; he died in office.

units.zh: 湛弟豹。
units.en: His younger brother was Bao.
units.literal: Zhan’s younger brother Bao.

units.zh: 湛弟豹
units.en: Yuan Bao, brother of Zhan.
units.literal: Zhan’s younger brother Bao.

units.zh: 湛弟豹
units.en: Yuan Bao.
units.literal: Zhan’s younger brother Bao.

units.zh: 豹字士蔚，博學善文辭，有經國材，為劉裕所知。
units.en: Yuan Bao, courtesy Shiwei, wrote well, knew the classics, showed administrative gifts, and impressed Liu Yu.
units.literal: Bao, courtesy name Shiwei, was broadly learned and skilled at prose, possessed talent for governing the state, and came to Liu Yu’s attention.

units.zh: 後為太尉長史、丹陽尹，卒。
units.en: He later served as chief of staff to the grand commandant and governor of Danyang, then died in office.
units.literal: Later he served as senior clerk to the grand commandant and Prefect of Danyang; he died.

units.zh: 江逌
units.en: Jiang You
units.literal: Jiang You

units.zh: 江逌，字道載，陳留圉人也。
units.en: Jiang You, courtesy Daozai, came from Yu county in Chenliu.
units.literal: Jiang You, courtesy name Daozai, was a native of Yu in Chenliu.

units.zh: 曾祖蕤，譙郡太守。
units.en: His great-grandfather Jiang Rui governed Qiao commandery.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Rui had been Administrator of Qiao Commandery.

units.zh: 祖允，蕪湖令。
units.en: His grandfather Yun had been Wuhu county magistrate.
units.literal: His grandfather Yun had been magistrate of Wuhu.

units.zh: 父濟，安東參軍。
units.en: His father Ji served on the staff of the eastern pacification general.
units.literal: His father Ji had been army adviser to the general pacifying the east.

units.zh: 逌少孤，與從弟灌共居，甚相友悌，由是獲當時之譽。
units.en: Orphaned early, he lived with cousin Jiang Guan in harmony and earned a reputation for fraternal devotion.
units.literal: You was orphaned young and lived with his cousin Guan; they were devoted brothers and thereby won contemporary praise.

units.zh: 避蘇峻之亂，屏居臨海，絕棄人事，翦茅結宇，耽玩載籍，有終焉之志。
units.en: When Su Jun threw the realm into chaos he withdrew to Linhai, shut out politics, built a thatched study, buried himself in texts, and meant to finish his life there.
units.literal: Fleeing Su Jun’s turmoil he withdrew to Linhai, cut himself off from worldly affairs, thatched a hut, reveled in books, and resolved to end his days there.

units.zh: 本州辟從事，除佐著作郎，並不就。
units.en: The province tried to hire him as aide and the court named him editorial assistant—he refused both.
units.literal: The province summoned him as aide and he was appointed editorial aide—he accepted neither.

units.zh: 征北將軍蔡謨命為參軍，何充復引為驃騎功曹。
units.en: Cai Mo took him as military adviser; He Chong later added him as merit clerk on the cavalry staff.
units.literal: General Who Conquers the North Cai Mo appointed him army adviser; He Chong again brought him in as merit clerk for the chariot-and-cavalry command.

units.zh: 以家貧，求試守，為太末令。
units.en: Pressed by poverty he sought an acting post and became magistrate of Taiwei.
units.literal: Because his household was poor he sought probationary appointment and became magistrate of Taiwei.

units.zh: 縣界深山中，有亡命數百家，恃險為阻，前後守宰莫能平。
units.en: Hundreds of outlaws held the mountain fastnesses—prefect after prefect failed to subdue them.
units.literal: Deep in the county mountains several hundred fugitives relied on rough terrain; successive magistrates could not pacify them.

units.zh: 逌到官，召其魁帥，厚加撫接，諭以禍福，旬月之間，繈負而至，朝廷嘉之。
units.en: You called in the bandit leaders, treated them generously, explained consequences, and within weeks families surrendered on his doorstep—the court commended him.
units.literal: When You arrived he summoned their chiefs, treated them generously, explained fortune and peril, and within a month they came carrying children on their backs—the court praised him.

units.zh: 州檄為治中，轉別駕，遷吳令。
units.en: He rose from provincial clerk to aide and then prefect of Wu county.
units.literal: The province ordered him administrator of records, then transferred him to provincial aide, then promoted him magistrate of Wu.

units.zh: 中軍將軍殷浩將謀北伐，請為諮議參軍。
units.en: When Yin Hao prepared to march north he asked You to join his staff as adviser.
units.literal: General of the Central Army Yin Hao planned a northern expedition and requested You as adviser on his staff.

units.zh: 浩甚重之，遷長史。
units.en: Yin Hao valued him and moved him up to chief clerk.
units.literal: Hao esteemed him highly and promoted him to chief clerk.

units.zh: 浩方修復洛陽，經營荒梗，逌為上佐，甚有匡弼之益，軍中書檄皆以委逌。
units.en: While Yin Hao rebuilt Luoyang from ruins You served as chief clerk with decisive help—every order and dispatch passed through him.
units.literal: As Hao restored Luoyang and worked the ruined wastes, You as chief aide offered strong corrective benefit; military orders and proclamations were all entrusted to You.

units.zh: 時羌及丁零叛，浩軍震懼。
units.en: When Qiang and Dingling auxiliaries mutinied Yin Hao’s army panicked.
units.literal: At that time Qiang and Dingling tribes rebelled and Hao’s army trembled with fear.

units.zh: 姚襄去浩十里結營以逼浩，浩令逌擊之。
units.en: Yao Xiang pitched camp ten li away to pin Yin Hao; Hao sent You to attack.
units.literal: Yao Xiang camped ten li from Hao to pressure him; Hao ordered You to strike.

units.zh: 逌進兵至襄營，謂將校曰：「今兵非不精，而衆少於羌，且其塹柵甚固，難與校力，吾當以計破之。」
units.en: Jiang You advanced on Yao Xiang’s camp and told his officers, “We are outnumbered and their earthworks are strong—a frontal contest will not serve; I must beat them by stratagem.”
units.literal: Jiang You advanced his troops to Yao Xiang’s camp and told the officers: “Our troops are not unfit, but we are fewer than the Qiang and their ditches and palisades are strong—hard to match strength head-on; I shall defeat them by stratagem.”

units.zh: 乃取數百雞以長繩連之，繫火於足。
units.en: He tied torches to hundreds of chickens on long cords.
units.literal: He therefore took several hundred chickens, tied them with long cords, and fastened torches to their feet.

units.zh: 群雞駭散，飛集襄營。
units.en: The terrified birds bolted into Yao Xiang’s camp.
units.literal: The flock panicked and scattered, flying into Xiang’s camp.

units.zh: 襄營火發，其亂，隨而擊之，襄遂小敗。
units.en: Flames erupted in the enemy camp; You charged into the chaos and handed Yao Xiang a partial defeat.
units.literal: Fire broke out in Xiang’s camp; amid the confusion You attacked and Xiang suffered a minor defeat.

units.zh: 及桓溫奏廢浩佐吏，遂免。
units.en: Huan Wen purged Yin Hao’s staff and You lost his post.
units.literal: When Huan Wen memorialized to dismiss Hao’s aides You was therefore removed.

units.zh: 頃之，除中書郎。
units.en: Soon he became a gentleman of the palace writers.
units.literal: Before long he was appointed gentleman of the palace secretariat.

units.zh: 升平中，遷吏部郎，長兼侍中。
units.en: Under Shengping he advanced to the Ministry of Personnel and served concurrently as palace attendant.
units.literal: During the Shengping era he rose to gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 穆帝將修後池，起閣道，逌上疏曰：
units.en: When Emperor Mu planned to enlarge the rear pond and raise a covered walkway You addressed the throne:
units.literal: Emperor Mu was about to renovate the rear pond and build a gallery bridge; You submitted a memorial saying:

units.zh: 帝嘉其言而止。
units.en: The emperor accepted his advice and dropped the project.
units.literal: The emperor praised his words and desisted.

units.zh: 復領本州大中正。
units.en: He resumed duty as senior locator for his home province.
units.literal: He again headed his province’s senior locator.

units.zh: 升平末，遷太常，逌累讓，不許。
units.en: Late in Shengping he became chamberlain for ceremonial rites—he tried to refuse repeatedly but the court insisted.
units.literal: Late in Shengping he was transferred to Chamberlain for Ceremonial; You repeatedly declined but was refused.

units.zh: 穆帝崩，山陵將用寶器，諫曰：「以宣皇顧命終制，山陵不設明器，以貽後則。
units.en: After Emperor Mu died ministers wanted rich tomb goods; You argued: “According to Emperor Xuan’s testamentary compact the mound must set out no bright vessels so as to hand down a model.
units.literal: When Emperor Mu died the imperial tomb was to employ precious grave goods; You remonstrated: “According to Emperor Xuan’s testamentary compact the mound must set out no bright vessels so as to hand down a model.

units.zh: 景帝奉遵遺制。
units.en: Emperor Jing obeyed that legacy.
units.literal: Emperor Jing followed the bequest.

units.zh: 逮文明皇后崩，武皇帝亦承前制，無所施設，惟脯脩之奠，瓦器而已。
units.en: When Empress Wenming passed away Emperor Wu likewise kept things austere—only dried meat and pottery vessels at the tomb.
units.literal: When Empress Wenming died Emperor Wu likewise continued prior models, setting out nothing except dried-meat offerings and earthen vessels.

units.zh: 昔康皇帝玄宮始用寶劍金舄，此蓋太妃罔已之情，實違先旨累世之法。
units.en: Emperor Kang’s burial first introduced jeweled blades and gold slippers—the grand consort’s unbounded grief overrode precedent and broke generations of restraint.
units.literal: Formerly Emperor Kang’s underground palace first used precious swords and gold slippers—this stemmed from the grand consort’s unbearable grief yet violated ancestral intent and generations of law.

units.zh: 今外欲以為故事，臣請述先旨，停此二物。」
units.en: Now officials want that excess as routine—You asked to reaffirm older restraint and ban both items.”
units.literal: Now those outside wish to treat it as precedent; I beg to rehearse prior intent and halt these two kinds of object.

units.zh: 書奏，從之。
units.en: The throne agreed.
units.literal: When the memorial arrived the court followed it.

units.zh: 哀帝以天文失度，欲依《尚書》洪祀之制，於太極前殿親執虔肅，冀以免咎，使太常集博士草其制。
units.en: Emperor Ai blamed heaven’s omens and wanted the Hong sacrifice from the 《Documents》 performed in the Taiji Hall—he would stand vigil himself—and told the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to draft rites with the boshi scholars.
units.literal: Emperor Ai, because celestial patterns were awry, wished to follow the Hong sacrifice protocol in the Documents at the forward hall of the Supreme Ultimate, personally maintaining reverent vigil in hope of averting blame; he ordered the Chamberlain for Ceremonial to gather erudits and draft the regulations.

units.zh: 逌上疏諫曰：
units.en: You filed a counter-memorial:
units.literal: You submitted a memorial remonstrating:

units.zh: 帝不納，逌又上疏曰：
units.en: The emperor brushed him off; You wrote again:
units.literal: The emperor did not accept it; You submitted again:

units.zh: 帝猶敕撰定，逌又陳古義，帝乃止。
units.en: The emperor still pressed for a codified rite until You cited classical precedent again and he gave up.
units.literal: The emperor still ordered compilation; You again presented classical precedents, and the emperor then stopped.

units.zh: 逌在職多所匡諫。
units.en: Throughout his tenure he remonstrated freely.
units.literal: While in office You often corrected and remonstrated.

units.zh: 著《阮籍序贊》、《逸士箴》及詩賦奏議數十篇行於世。
units.en: He wrote essays such as 《Preface and Encomium for Ruan Ji》 and 《Admonition for Recluses》, plus dozens of poems, rhapsodies, and memorials that circulated widely.
units.literal: He authored “Preface and Encomium for Ruan Ji,” “Admonition for Recluses,” and several tens of poems, fu, and memorials that circulated in the world.

units.zh: 病卒，時年五十八。
units.en: He died of illness at fifty-eight.
units.literal: He died of illness at age fifty-eight.

units.zh: 子蔚，吳興太守。
units.en: His son Jiang Wei governed Wuxing.
units.literal: His son Wei served as Administrator of Wuxing.

units.zh: 從弟灌
units.en: Jiang Guan, You’s younger cousin.
units.literal: Younger cousin Guan.

units.zh: 從弟灌
units.en: Jiang Guan.
units.literal: Younger cousin Guan.

units.zh: 灌字道群。
units.en: Guan used the courtesy name Daoqun.
units.literal: Guan, courtesy name Daoqun.

units.zh: 父瞢，尚書郎。
units.en: His father Meng once served as a gentleman clerk in the secretariat.
units.literal: His father Meng had been a gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 灌少知名，才識亞於逌。
units.en: Guan won notice early—second only to Jiang You in reputation.
units.literal: Guan was known young; his talent and insight ranked just below You’s.

units.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，為治中，轉別駕，歷司徒屬、北中郎中長史，領晉陵太守。
units.en: He rose from provincial recorder and aide to posts under the minister of education and chief clerk of the northern palace section, doubling as Jinling prefect.
units.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk; he passed the provincial examination; he served as administrator of records, transferred to provincial aide, successively served as secretary under the minister of education, senior clerk to the north-center section chief, and concurrent Administrator of Jinling.

units.zh: 簡文帝引為撫軍從事中郎，後遷吏部郎。
units.en: Emperor Jianwen named him senior attendant on the pacification staff; he later joined the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: Emperor Jianwen brought him in as attendant gentleman-in-chief on the pacification army staff; later he rose to gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 時謝奕為尚書，銓敘不允，灌每執正不從，奕托以他事免之，受黜無怨色。
units.en: When Xie Yi ran personnel assignments unfairly Guan held the line—Yi cashiered him on a pretext, but Guan accepted it without complaint.
units.literal: At that time Xie Yi was minister; personnel judgments were unfair; Guan often upheld rectitude and refused to comply; Yi found another excuse to dismiss him, yet he bore demotion without resentment.

units.zh: 頃之，簡文帝又以為撫軍司馬，甚相賓禮。
units.en: Soon Emperor Jianwen made him marshal of the pacification army and honored him lavishly.
units.literal: Before long Emperor Jianwen again appointed him marshal of the pacification army and treated him with great courtesy.

units.zh: 遷御史中丞，轉吳興太守。
units.en: He advanced to imperial censor then prefect of Wuxing.
units.literal: He was promoted to palace assistant censor and transferred to Administrator of Wuxing.

units.zh: 灌性方正，視權貴蔑如也，為大司馬桓溫所惡。
units.en: Upright to a fault, Guan snubbed power brokers—Huan Wen detested him.
units.literal: Guan’s nature was upright; he treated mighty nobles with contempt and Grand Marshal Huan Wen loathed him.

units.zh: 溫欲中傷之，徵拜侍中，以在郡時公事有失，追免之。
units.en: Huan Wen tried to trap him—summoned him as palace attendant, then dredged up prefectural paperwork to dismiss him.
units.literal: Wen wished to ruin him: he summoned him as palace attendant and then, citing administrative faults while in commandery office, stripped him retroactively.

units.zh: 後為秘書監，尋復解職。
units.en: He briefly headed the palace library then stepped down.
units.literal: Later he became secretary supervisor but soon resigned.

units.zh: 時溫方執權，朝廷希旨，故灌積年不調。
units.en: With Huan Wen dominating court appointments Guan languished without a new post.
units.literal: At that time Wen held power and the court followed his lead; therefore Guan went years without reassignment.

units.zh: 溫末年，以為諮議參軍。
units.en: Late in life Huan Wen relented and named him staff adviser.
units.literal: In Wen’s last years he appointed him adviser on staff.

units.zh: 會溫薨，遷尚書、中護軍，復出為吳郡太守，加秩中二千石，未拜，卒。
units.en: After Huan Wen died Guan climbed to minister and Defender of the Center, returned as Wu prefect with top salary—and died before the seal arrived.
units.literal: When Wen died Guan rose to minister and Defender of the Center, again went out as Administrator of Wu Commandery, was slated for salary of two thousand shi plus rank, but died before investiture.

units.zh: 子績。
units.en: His heir was Jiang Ji.
units.literal: Son Ji.

units.zh: 灌子績
units.en: Jiang Ji, Guan’s son.
units.literal: Guan’s son Ji.

units.zh: 灌子績
units.en: Jiang Ji.
units.literal: Guan’s son Ji.

units.zh: 績字仲元，有志氣，除秘書郎。
units.en: Ji bore the courtesy name Zhongyuan, showed backbone, and became a palace secretary.
units.literal: Ji, courtesy name Zhongyuan, had strong resolve and was appointed secretary gentleman.

units.zh: 以父與謝氏不穆，故謝安之世辟召無所從，論者多之。
units.en: His father’s feud with the Xie meant Ji ignored every summons while Xie An lived—opinion admired his stance.
units.literal: Because his father was estranged from the Xie clan, during Xie An’s lifetime summoning orders never found acceptance—critics praised him.

units.zh: 安薨，始為會稽王道子驃騎主簿，多所規諫。
units.en: Once Xie An died he joined Prince Daozi of Kuaiji as cavalry chief clerk and spoke truth to power.
units.literal: After An died he first served Prince Kuaiji Daozi as chief clerk of the cavalry command and often remonstrated.

units.zh: 歷諮議參軍，出為南郡相。
units.en: He advised princes and then governed Nan commandery.
units.literal: He served as adviser on staff and went out as chancellor of Nan Commandery.

units.zh: 會荊州刺史殷仲堪舉兵以應王恭，仲堪要績與南蠻校尉殷顗同行，並不從。
units.en: When Yin Zhongkan mobilized to support Wang Gong he insisted Ji travel with Yin Yi—both men refused.
units.literal: When Inspector of Jing Yin Zhongkan raised troops to answer Wang Gong, Zhongkan pressed Ji to travel with Southern Man Colonel Yin Yi—both refused.

units.zh: 仲堪等屢以為言，績終不為之屈。
units.en: Yin Zhongkan kept demanding; Ji never bent.
units.literal: Zhongkan and others repeatedly pressed the point; Ji never yielded.

units.zh: 顗慮績及禍，乃于仲堪坐和解之。
units.en: Yin Yi feared bloodshed and mediated at Zhongkan’s banquet.
units.literal: Yi feared Ji would court disaster and at Zhongkan’s banquet mediated.

units.zh: 績曰：「大丈夫何至以死相脅！
units.en: Ji snapped, “Must a gentleman threaten death?
units.literal: Ji said: “How could a great man threaten another with death!

units.zh: 江仲元行年六十，但未知獲死所耳。」
units.en: Jiang Zhongyuan is sixty—I only wonder where I shall fall.”
units.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan is sixty years old—I simply do not yet know where I shall die.”

units.zh: 一坐為之懼。
units.en: The table fell silent in dread.
units.literal: The whole company feared on his account.

units.zh: 仲堪憚其堅正，以楊佺期代之。
units.en: Zhongkan, unnerved by his steel, swapped him for Yang Quanqi.
units.literal: Zhongkan dreaded his firm integrity and replaced him with Yang Quanqi.

units.zh: 朝廷聞而征績為御史中丞，奏劾無所屈撓。
units.en: The court recalled him as censor—his indictments showed no favor.
units.literal: The court heard and summoned Ji as palace assistant censor; his impeachments bowed to none.

units.zh: 會稽世子元顯專政，夜開六門，績密啟會稽王道子，欲以奏聞，道子不許。
units.en: When the heir apparent of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, seized power and opened the six palace gates at night Ji secretly urged Prince Daozi to report it—Daozi refused.
units.literal: The heir apparent of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, monopolized power, opening the six gates by night; Ji secretly informed Prince Daozi of Kuaiji wishing to memorialize; Daozi forbade it.

units.zh: 車胤亦曰：「元顯驕縱，宜禁制之。」
units.en: Che Yin added, “Yuanxian’s arrogance must be curbed.”
units.literal: Che Yin also said: “Yuanxian is arrogant and unrestrained; he should be restrained.”

units.zh: 道子默然。
units.en: Daozi said nothing.
units.literal: Daozi was silent.

units.zh: 元顯聞而謂衆曰：「江績、車胤間我父子。」
units.en: Yuanxian heard and announced, “Jiang Ji and Che Yin are splitting my father and me.”
units.literal: Yuanxian heard and told the assembly: “Jiang Ji and Che Yin drive a wedge between me and my father.”

units.zh: 遣人密讓之。
units.en: He sent agents to reprimand them quietly.
units.literal: He sent men secretly to rebuke them.

units.zh: 俄而績卒，朝野悼之。
units.en: Ji died soon after; capital and countryside mourned.
units.literal: Soon Ji died; court and countryside mourned him.

units.zh: 車胤
units.en: Che Yin
units.literal: Che Yin

units.zh: 車胤，字武子，南平人也。
units.en: Che Yin, courtesy Wuzi, hailed from Nanping.
units.literal: Che Yin, courtesy name Wuzi, was a native of Nanping.

units.zh: 曾祖浚，吳會稽太守。
units.en: His great-grandfather Jun governed Kuaiji under Wu.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Jun had been Administrator of Kuaiji under Wu.

units.zh: 父育，郡主簿。
units.en: His father Yu served as county recorder.
units.literal: His father Yu had been county chief clerk.

units.zh: 太守王胡之名知人，見胤于童幼之中，謂胤父曰：「此兒當大興卿門，可使專學。」
units.en: Prefect Wang Huzhi sized him up in the schoolyard and told his father, “This child will glorify your line—let him study.”
units.literal: Prefect Wang Huzhi was famed for judging men; seeing Yin among children he told Yin’s father: “This boy will greatly exalt your house—have him devote himself to study.”

units.zh: 胤恭勤不倦，博學多通。
units.en: Che Yin studied tirelessly and mastered many disciplines.
units.literal: Yin was respectful and diligent without weariness; he was broadly learned and mastered many subjects.

units.zh: 家貧不常得油，夏月則練囊盛數十螢火以照書，以夜繼日焉。
units.en: Too poor for lamp oil, he stuffed fireflies in a silk bag to read by night—the famous “firefly glow” diligence.
units.literal: His household was poor and could not always obtain lamp oil; in summer he packed dozens of fireflies in a silk sack to illuminate his books, continuing day into night.

units.zh: 及長，風姿美劭，機悟敏速，甚有鄉曲之譽。
units.en: Grown handsome and sharp, he won wide local fame.
units.literal: When grown he was handsome and alert, quick and perceptive, and enjoyed great local renown.

units.zh: 桓溫在荊州，辟為從事，以辯識義理深重之。
units.en: Huan Wen in Jingzhou hired him as aide and prized his grasp of principle.
units.literal: When Huan Wen was in Jing Province he summoned Yin as aide and deeply valued him for debating principles.

units.zh: 引為主簿，稍遷別駕、征西長史，遂顯於朝廷。
units.en: He rose from chief clerk to provincial aide and western campaign chief clerk—then made his name at court.
units.literal: He brought him in as chief clerk and gradually promoted him to provincial aide and chief clerk of the western expedition; thus he became eminent at court.

units.zh: 時惟胤與吳隱之以寒素博學知名於世。
units.en: Only Che Yin and Wu Yinzhi were celebrated for rising from cold households through scholarship.
units.literal: At the time only Yin and Wu Yinzhi were famed for humble origins yet broad learning.

units.zh: 又善於賞會，當時每有盛坐而胤不在，皆云：「無車公不樂。」
units.en: He hosted surpassingly well—guests swore no feast sparkled without “Lord Che.”
units.literal: He also excelled at hosting gatherings; whenever there was a splendid banquet without Yin, all said, “Without Lord Che there is no joy.”

units.zh: 謝安遊集之日，輒開筵待之。
units.en: Whenever Xie An entertained he saved a seat for Che Yin.
units.literal: Whenever Xie An held outings he always spread a feast and awaited him.

units.zh: 甯康初，以胤為中書侍郎、關內侯。
units.en: Early in Ningkang he became palace secretary and marquis within the passes.
units.literal: In the early Ningkang era Yin was appointed gentleman of the palace secretariat and marquis within the passes.

units.zh: 孝武帝嘗講《孝經》，僕射謝安侍坐，尚書陸納侍講，侍中卞眈執讀，黃門侍郎謝石、吏部郎袁宏執經，胤與丹陽尹王混擿句，時論榮之。
units.en: When Emperor Xiaowu expounded the 《Classic of Filial Piety》, Xie An, Lu Na, Bian Dan, Xie Shi, Yuan Hong, Che Yin, and Wang Hun each played a ceremonial role—the age deemed it glory.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu once lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety: Vice Director Xie An sat in attendance, Minister Lu Na attended the exposition, Palace Attendant Bian Dan held the text, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Xie Shi and Gentleman in Personnel Yuan Hong held the classics, while Yin and Prefect of Danyang Wang Hun parsed lines—opinion of the time honored them.

units.zh: 累遷侍中。
units.en: He advanced stepwise to palace attendant.
units.literal: He rose through successive posts to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 太元中，增置太學生百人，以胤領國子博士。
units.en: During the Taiyuan era they added a hundred National Academy students and placed Yin in charge as erudite of the National University.
units.literal: During the Taiyuan era they added a hundred National Academy students and placed Yin in charge as erudite of the National University.

units.zh: 其後年，議郊廟明堂之事，胤以「明堂之制既甚難詳，且樂主於和，禮主於敬，故質文不同，音器亦殊。
units.en: Next year, arguing suburban rites and the Bright Hall, Che Yin began: “Bright Hall layout is notoriously elusive; music pursues harmony, ritual pursues reverence, so form and ornament diverge and bells and vessels cannot match.
units.literal: The following year, debating suburban altars and the Bright Hall, Yin argued that “the Bright Hall system is already hard to pin down, and since music aims at harmony while ritual aims at reverence, substance and ornament differ and therefore tones and vessels diverge.

units.zh: 既茅茨廣廈不一其度，何必守其形範而不弘本順時乎！
units.en: Thatched cottages and marble halls follow different scales—why fetishize shape rather than grasp the essence and move with the times?
units.literal: Since thatched huts and grand halls do not share one measure, why cling to mere outward models instead of honoring the root and following the season?

units.zh: 九服咸寧，四野無塵，然後明堂辟雍可光而修之。」
units.en: Wait until the realm is quiet and dust-free across the frontiers—then you may splendidly rebuild Bright Hall and the royal academy.”
units.literal: Only when the nine circuits are calm and the four wildernesses bear no dust may one gloriously restore the Bright Hall and Biyong.

units.zh: 時從其議。
units.en: The court adopted his view.
units.literal: At the time the court followed his proposal.

units.zh: 又遷驃騎長史、太常，進爵臨湘侯，以疾去職。
units.en: He rose to cavalry chief clerk and chamberlain for rites, became marquis of Linxiang, then resigned ill.
units.literal: He was further promoted chief clerk of the chariot-and-cavalry command and Chamberlain for Ceremonial, advanced to Marquis of Linxiang, then left office owing to illness.

units.zh: 俄為護軍將軍。
units.en: Soon he commanded the Defender-in-Chief army.
units.literal: Before long he served as Defender-in-Chief.

units.zh: 時王國寶諂于會稽王道子，諷八坐啟以道子為丞相，加殊禮。
units.en: Wang Guobao curried favor with Prince Daozi of Kuaiji and coached the Eight Seats to ask that Daozi become chancellor with superlative ceremony.
units.literal: At that time Wang Guobao flattered Prince Daozi of Kuaiji and prompted the Eight Seats to memorialize making Daozi chancellor with extraordinary honors.

units.zh: 胤曰：「此乃成王所以尊周公也。
units.en: Che Yin replied, “Such honors fit how the young king deferred to the Duke of Zhou.
units.literal: Yin said: “That is how the youthful king honored the Duke of Zhou.

units.zh: 今主上當陽，非成王之地，相王在位，豈得為周公乎！
units.en: Our emperor sits openly on the throne—not a minor regency—and the prince regent is no Duke of Zhou.
units.literal: Now the sovereign faces south—this is not the youthful king’s situation—and the prince regent holds office—how can he equal the Duke of Zhou!

units.zh: 望實二三，並不宜爾，必大忤上意。」
units.en: Neither prestige nor substance warrants this—it will only insult the emperor.”
units.literal: Their reputations fall short two or threefold in both deed and reality—none of this fits and will surely deeply offend the throne.

units.zh: 乃稱疾不署其事。
units.en: He feigned sickness and withheld his signature.
units.literal: He therefore pleaded illness and refused to endorse the document.

units.zh: 疏奏，帝大怒，而甚嘉胤。
units.en: The emperor raged at the proposal but applauded Che Yin.
units.literal: When the memorial arrived the emperor was furious yet deeply praised Yin.

units.zh: 隆安初，為吳興太守，秩中二千石，辭疾不拜。
units.en: Early in Longan they named him Wuxing prefect at top salary—he pleaded illness and refused.
units.literal: In the early Longan era he was appointed Administrator of Wuxing at salary of two thousand shi—he declined citing illness.

units.zh: 加輔國將軍、丹陽尹。
units.en: They added titles as supporting-state general and Danyang prefect.
units.literal: He was additionally General Who Supports the State and Prefect of Danyang.

units.zh: 頃之，遷吏部尚書。
units.en: Soon he headed the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: Before long he rose to Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 元顯有過，胤與江績密言于道子，將奏之，事泄，元顯逼令自裁。
units.en: When Yuanxian misbehaved Che Yin and Jiang Ji whispered to Daozi about impeachment—word slipped out and Yuanxian drove Che Yin to suicide.
units.literal: Yuanxian erred; Yin and Jiang Ji spoke secretly to Daozi planning to memorialize; the affair leaked and Yuanxian forced him to kill himself.

units.zh: 俄而胤卒，朝廷傷之。
