units.en: Che Yin died shortly after; the court grieved.
units.literal: Soon Yin died and the court mourned him.

units.zh: 殷顗
units.en: Yin Yi
units.literal: Yin Yi

units.zh: 殷顗，字伯通，陳郡人也。
units.en: Yin Yi, courtesy Botong, came from Chen commandery.
units.literal: Yin Yi, courtesy name Botong, was a native of Chen Commandery.

units.zh: 祖融，太常卿。
units.en: His grandfather Yin Rong led the Chamberlain’s office.
units.literal: His grandfather Rong had been Chamberlain for Ceremonial.

units.zh: 父康，吳興太守。
units.en: His father Kang governed Wuxing.
units.literal: His father Kang had been Administrator of Wuxing.

units.zh: 顗性通率，有才氣，少與從弟仲堪俱知名。
units.en: Yi was open-hearted and gifted—celebrated alongside cousin Yin Zhongkan in youth.
units.literal: Yi was frank and generous by nature, talented, and in youth shared fame with his cousin Zhongkan.

units.zh: 太元中，以中書郎擢為南蠻校尉。
units.en: Under Taiyuan he jumped from palace secretary to southern tribes colonel.
units.literal: During the Taiyuan era he rose from gentleman of the palace secretariat to Colonel of the Southern Man.

units.zh: 蒞職清明，政績肅舉。
units.en: His rule stayed clean and crisp.
units.literal: His tenure was lucid and his administration sternly effective.

units.zh: 及仲堪得王恭書，將興兵內伐，告顗，欲同舉。
units.en: When Zhongkan got Wang Gong’s letter plotting an attack on the capital he told Yi and wanted joint action.
units.literal: When Zhongkan received Wang Gong’s letter and planned to raise troops inward against the court he informed Yi and wished to act together.

units.zh: 顗不平之，曰：「夫人臣之義，慎保所守。
units.en: Yi bridled: “Ministers must guard their posts.
units.literal: Yi was displeased and said: “The duty of a minister is carefully to guard what he holds.

units.zh: 朝廷是非，宰輔之務，豈籓屏之所圖也。
units.en: Court disputes belong to the chief ministers—not frontier intendants.
units.literal: Right and wrong at court are the chief ministers’ business—how can a screen prince scheme them?

units.zh: 晉陽之事，宜所不豫。」
units.en: 'Jinyang-style' coups are none of your business.”
units.literal: Affairs like the Jinyang expedition are not what you should join.

units.zh: 仲堪要之轉切，顗怒曰：「吾進不敢同，退不敢異。」
units.en: Zhongkan doubled down; Yi snapped, “I will neither march with you nor scheme against you.”
units.literal: Zhongkan pressed harder; Yi angrily said: “Advancing I dare not join you; retreating I dare not oppose you.”

units.zh: 仲堪以為恨。
units.en: Zhongkan never forgave him.
units.literal: Zhongkan nursed resentment.

units.zh: 猶密諫仲堪，辭甚切至。
units.en: Yi still slipped Zhongkan urgent secret warnings.
units.literal: Yi still secretly remonstrated Zhongkan with utmost earnestness.

units.zh: 仲堪既貴，素情亦殊，而志望無厭，謂顗言為非。
units.en: Power changed Zhongkan—his appetite grew and he dismissed Yi’s counsel.
units.literal: Once Zhongkan grew powerful his temperament changed and ambition knew no satiety; he deemed Yi’s words wrong.

units.zh: 顗見江績亦以正直為仲堪所斥，知仲堪當逐異己，樹置所親，因出行散，托疾不還。
units.en: Watching Jiang Ji cashiered for honesty Yi knew Zhongkan would purge outsiders—he left on “walking powder,” claimed illness, and stayed away.
units.literal: Seeing Jiang Ji likewise expelled for integrity, Yi knew Zhongkan would purge dissenters and plant favorites; he therefore went out to take walking powder, pleaded illness, and did not return.

units.zh: 仲堪聞其病，出省之，謂顗曰：「兄病殊為可憂。」
units.en: Zhongkan visited his sickbed and said, “Brother, this sickness frightens me.”
units.literal: Zhongkan heard of his illness and went out to console him, telling Yi: “Elder brother, your illness truly worries me.”

units.zh: 顗曰：「我病不過身死，但汝病在滅門，幸熟為慮，勿以我為念也。」
units.en: Yi answered, “My worst is death; yours is clan extinction—think about yourself, not me.”
units.literal: Yi said: “My sickness goes no further than my death, but yours threatens your entire clan—think hard and do not fret over me.”

units.zh: 仲堪不從，卒與楊佺期、桓玄同下。
units.en: Zhongkan ignored him and marched east with Yang Quanqi and Huan Xuan.
units.literal: Zhongkan did not listen and ultimately descended east with Yang Quanqi and Huan Xuan.

units.zh: 顗遂以憂卒。
units.en: Yi died of sorrow.
units.literal: Yi therefore died of grief.

units.zh: 隆安中，詔曰：「故南蠻校尉殷顗忠績未融，奄焉隕喪，可贈冠軍將軍。」
units.en: In mid Longan an edict stated: “The late Colonel of the Southern Man Yin Yi’s loyal merit never ripened before he suddenly passed—posthumously appoint him General Who Champions the Army.”
units.literal: In mid Longan an edict stated: “The late Colonel of the Southern Man Yin Yi’s loyal merit never ripened before he suddenly passed—posthumously appoint him General Who Champions the Army.”

units.zh: 弟仲文、叔獻別有傳。
units.en: His brothers Yin Zhongwen and Yin Shuxian appear elsewhere.
units.literal: Younger brothers Zhongwen and Shuxian have separate biographies.

units.zh: 王雅
units.en: Wang Ya
units.literal: Wang Ya

units.zh: 王雅，字茂達，東海郯人，魏衛將軍肅之曾孫也。
units.en: Wang Ya, courtesy Maoda, came from Tan in Donghai—descended from Wang Su, Wei’s Guard General.
units.literal: Wang Ya, courtesy name Maoda, was a native of Tan in Donghai and great-grandson of Wei General Who Guards the Right Wang Su.

units.zh: 祖隆，後將軍。
units.en: His grandfather Long commanded the rear army.
units.literal: His grandfather Long had been General of the Rear.

units.zh: 父景，大鴻臚。
units.en: His father Jing served as grand herald.
units.literal: His father Jing had been Grand Herald.

units.zh: 雅少知名，州檄主簿，舉秀才，除郎中，出補永興令，以幹理著稱。
units.en: Wang Ya rose early—provincial aide, examination graduate, gentleman, Yongxing magistrate—with a reputation for competence.
units.literal: Ya was known young; the province summoned him chief clerk; he passed the examination; he was appointed gentleman; went out as magistrate of Yongxing— famed for capable administration.

units.zh: 累遷尚書左右丞，歷廷尉、侍中、左衛將軍、丹陽尹，領太子左衛率。
units.en: He climbed to assistant ministers of the secretariat, commandant of justice, palace attendant, general guarding the left, Danyang prefect, plus commander of the heir’s left guard.
units.literal: He rose through successive posts to Left and Right Assistant Minister of the Masters of Writing, served as commandant of justice, palace attendant, General Who Guards the Left, Prefect of Danyang, and concurrently commanded the heir’s left guard.

units.zh: 雅性好接下，敬慎奉公，孝武帝深加禮遇，雖在外職，侍見甚數，朝廷大事多參謀議。
units.en: Wang Ya welcomed junior officers, served carefully, and enjoyed Emperor Xiaowu’s trust—despite outside duties he advised constantly on state matters.
units.literal: Ya loved receiving inferiors; he was reverent and cautious in public service; Emperor Xiaowu deeply favored him—although holding outside posts he was summoned often and participated widely in great affairs.

units.zh: 帝每置酒宴集，雅未至，不先舉觴，其見重如此。
units.en: At every banquet the emperor waited for Wang Ya before drinking—such was his standing.
units.literal: Whenever the emperor held banquets he would not lift his cup until Ya arrived—such was the esteem.

units.zh: 然任遇有過其才，時人被以佞幸之目。
units.en: Yet rewards outstripped ability—critics called him a court favorite.
units.literal: Yet favor exceeded his talent; contemporaries labeled him sycophantic.

units.zh: 帝起清暑殿于後宮，開北上閣，出華林園，與美人張氏同遊止，惟雅與焉。
units.en: The emperor built Cool Summer Palace, opened a back gate into Hualin Garden, and toured with Lady Zhang—only Wang Ya joined.
units.literal: The emperor built the Cool Summer Palace in the rear palace, opened the northern upper gate to exit Hualin Garden, and roamed and lodged with the beauty Lady Zhang—only Ya accompanied him.

units.zh: 會稽王道子領太子太傅，以雅為太子少傅。
units.en: Prince Daozi of Kuaiji led the heir’s tutorship and named Wang Ya junior tutor.
units.literal: Prince Daozi of Kuaiji headed the heir’s grand tutorate and appointed Ya Junior Tutor to the heir.

units.zh: 時王珣兒婚，賓客車騎甚衆，會聞雅拜少傅，回詣雅者過半。
units.en: During Wang Xun’s son’s wedding crowds jammed the roads—but half wheeled away once Wang Ya’s junior tutor appointment broke.
units.literal: At that time Wang Xun’s son married; guests and carriages thronged—when word spread that Ya had been named junior tutor more than half turned back to visit Ya.

units.zh: 時風俗頹弊，無復廉恥。
units.en: Manners had rotted beyond embarrassment.
units.literal: Custom was decadent beyond shame.

units.zh: 然少傅之任，朝望屬珣，珣亦頗以自幸。
units.en: Everyone had expected Wang Xun to win the post—and Xun counted on it.
units.literal: Yet court expectation had pinned the junior tutor post on Xun, and Xun himself rather fancied the honor.

units.zh: 及中詔用雅，衆遂赴雅焉。
units.en: When the edict picked Wang Ya the crowd rushed to him.
units.literal: When the palace edict chose Ya the multitude flocked to Ya instead.

units.zh: 將拜，遇雨，請以傘入。
units.en: Rain soaked investiture day; he asked to carry an umbrella indoors.
units.literal: About to be invested, rain fell; he requested to enter with an umbrella.

units.zh: 王珣不許之，因冒雨而拜。
units.en: Wang Xun refused—Wang Ya took the ritual soaked to the skin.
units.literal: Wang Xun forbade it, so he underwent investiture through the rain.

units.zh: 雅既貴幸，威權甚震，門下車騎常數百，而善應接，傾心禮之。
units.en: Power swelled his salon to hundreds of carriages—yet he greeted each petitioner graciously.
units.literal: Once Ya grew favored his authority awed others—hundreds of carriages filled his gate—yet he courteously received everyone who sought him.

units.zh: 帝以道子無社稷器幹，慮晏駕之後皇室傾危，乃選時望以為籓屏，將擢王恭、殷仲堪等，先以訪雅。
units.en: Fearing Prince Daozi too weak to guard the dynasty, Emperor Xiaowu picked reputable buffers—Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan—and asked Wang Ya first.
units.literal: Because Daozi lacked capacity to shoulder the altars the emperor feared peril to the house after his death; he therefore chose leading reputations as bulwarks and planned to elevate Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan—first he consulted Ya.

units.zh: 雅以恭等無當世之才，不可大任，從容曰：「王恭風神簡貴，志氣方嚴，既居外戚之重，當親賢之寄，然其稟性峻隘，無所苞容，執自是之操，無守節之志。
units.en: Wang Ya thought them unfit: “Wang Gong looks noble and acts severe—as imperial in-law he shoulders heavy trust—yet he is cramped, unforgiving, stubborn, and unreliable.
units.literal: Ya judged Gong and others lacking talent for the age and unsuited to heavy duty; calmly he said: “Wang Gong’s bearing is refined and lofty, his resolve stern—already burdened as maternal kin and entrusted as intimate—yet his nature is narrow and admits no breadth; he clings to self-righteousness and lacks constancy.

units.zh: 仲堪雖謹於細行，以文義著稱，亦無弘量，且幹略不長。
units.en: Zhongkan fusses petty detail and literary fame yet lacks breadth or strategic depth.
units.literal: Zhongkan, though meticulous in small conduct and famed for literary taste, likewise lacks breadth and moreover short strategic grasp.

units.zh: 若委以連率之重，據形勝之地，今四海無事，足能守職，若道不常隆，必為亂階矣。」
units.en: Give them frontier supremacy while peace lasts they might cope—if fortune falters they become rebellion itself.”
units.literal: If you entrust them with governor-general weight and strategic terrain, while the realm is calm they may suffice—but if the Way does not remain prosperous they will become seeds of rebellion.”

units.zh: 帝以恭等為當時秀望，謂雅疾其勝己，故不從。
units.en: The emperor thought Wang Gong’s circle the best of the age and assumed Wang Ya jealous—so he ignored him.
units.literal: The emperor deemed Gong and others the leading talents of the moment and supposed Ya envied their superiority—therefore he did not listen.

units.zh: 二人皆被升用，其後竟敗，有識之士稱其知人。
units.en: Both rose—and later fell—while wise men credited Wang Ya’s insight.
units.literal: Both men were promoted and afterward indeed failed—knowing observers praised his judgment of men.

units.zh: 遷領軍、尚書、散騎常侍，方大崇進之，將參副相之重，而帝崩，倉卒不獲顧命。
units.en: He neared minister and defender posts—then the emperor died suddenly without naming him regent.
units.literal: He rose to command the armies, minister, gentleman at the palace gate—great advancement was planned with deputy chief minister rank—then the emperor died and hasty circumstances denied a testament.

units.zh: 雅素被優遇，一旦失權，又以朝廷方亂，內外攜離，但慎默而已，無所辯正。
units.en: Long favored, Wang Ya lost leverage overnight as chaos split court—he stayed mute.
units.literal: Ya had long enjoyed favor; once power vanished and court turmoil tore inside from outside he kept cautious silence and corrected nothing.

units.zh: 雖在孝武世，亦不能犯顏廷爭，凡所謀謨，唯唯而已。
units.en: Even under Xiaowu he rarely debated openly—always nodding yes.
units.literal: Even under Emperor Xiaowu he had not dared argue face to face at court; every stratagem he merely assented to.

units.zh: 尋遷左僕射。
units.en: Soon he became left vice director.
units.literal: Soon he rose to Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 隆安四年卒，時年六十七。
units.en: In the fourth year of Long'an, he died at sixty-seven.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, he died at age sixty-seven.

units.zh: 追贈光祿大夫、儀同三司。
units.en: Posthumously named grand master of brilliant splendor with honors matching the Three Ducal Ministers.
units.literal: Posthumously honored Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor, Unequaled in Honor.

units.zh: 長子准之，散騎侍郎。
units.en: His eldest Zhunzhi served as palace presenter.
units.literal: Eldest son Zhunzhi, Gentleman for Palace Presentation.

units.zh: 次協之，黃門。
units.en: Second son Xiezhi worked the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: Second Xiezhi, Yellow Gate.

units.zh: 次少卿，侍中。
units.en: Third son Shaoqing became palace attendant.
units.literal: Third Shaoqing, Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 並有士操，立名於世云。
units.en: All kept gentlemanly reputations.
units.literal: All possessed gentlemen’s conduct and established names in the world.

units.zh: 史評
units.en: Historians’ commentary
units.literal: Historians’ appraisal

units.zh: 史臣曰：爰在中興，玄風滋扇，溺王綱於拱默，撓國步於清虛，骨鯁蹇諤之風蓋亦微矣。
units.en: The historian writes: Under the restored court “dark learning” numbed government—honest criticism nearly vanished.
units.literal: The historian says: At the eastern restoration abstruse winds blew stronger—drowning royal norms in idle silence, stumbling the state march in empty purity—forthright remonstrance grew scarce indeed.

units.zh: 而君孝固情禮而違顯命，山甫獻誠讜而振頹風，彥叔之兵謀，道載之正諫，洋洋盈耳，有足可稱。
units.en: Still Gu He defied summons for mourning’s sake; Shanfu offered sincere counsel to revive a declining ethos; Yuan Qiao planned campaigns; Jiang You spoke plain truth—all merit praise.
units.literal: Yet Junxiao clung to feeling and ritual against shining mandates; Shanfu offered sincere counsel to revive a decadent wind; Yanshu’s military schemes and Daozai’s upright remonstrance ring richly—worthy of praise.

units.zh: 灌不屈節於權臣，績敢危言於賊將，道子殊物之禮，車胤沮之無懼心，仲堪反常之舉，殷顗折之以正色，求諸古烈，何以加焉！
units.en: Jiang Guan refused cronies; Jiang Ji defied warlords; Che Yin thwarted Daozi’s excess; Yin Yi stared down Zhongkan—few ancients outdid them.
units.literal: Guan bent no knee to power brokers; Ji dared bold words to rebel generals; Daozi’s extraordinary honors Che Yin blocked without fear; Zhongkan’s irregular plots Yin Yi broke with stern integrity—set beside ancient paragons, what could surpass them?

units.zh: 山松悅哀挽於軒冕之辰，彥道歡博徒於衰絰之日，天心已喪，其能濟乎！
units.en: Yuan Shansong sang dirges in silk hats; Yuan Dan diced in mourning clothes—hearts were dead—how expect salvation?
units.literal: Shansong took pleasure in laments amid court finery; Yandao reveled with gamblers while wearing mourning—heaven’s mind already lost—how could they prosper!

units.zh: 旋及於促齡，俄致於非命，宜哉！
units.en: They died young or violently—justice enough.
units.literal: Soon they met early death or violent ends—fitting indeed!

units.zh: 贊曰：顧生軌物，屢申誠讜。
units.en: Verse praise: Gu He set standards and spoke truth.
units.literal: Encomium: Master Gu regulated conduct and repeatedly voiced sincere counsel.

units.zh: 袁子崇儒，拯斯頹喪。
units.en: Master Yuan upheld Confucius against collapse.
units.literal: Master Yuan upheld Confucian learning and rescued that decadent wasteland.

units.zh: 逌績剛蹇，車殷忠壯。
units.en: Jiang You and Jiang Ji stood firm; Che Yin and Yin Yi showed courage.
units.literal: You and Ji were rigidly upright; Che and Yin loyal and bold.

units.zh: 睠言遺直，莫之能尚。
units.en: Remembering such upright survivors, none rank higher.
units.literal: Turning to these lingering exemplars, none can surpass them.
